#2869. Nets blow past Pelicans with an offensive resurgence, win 145-111

After their hardest hitting loss of the season, the Big Easy was the perfect place for the Brooklyn Nets to go next on their road trip. The Nets obliterated the New Orleans Pelicans this evening at the Smoothie King Center. Few wins have been more necessary, and even fewer more deserved.

However, the contest wasn't advertised as the breakaway layup it turned into.

The Pelicans were at home, and with a Zion Williamson coming off three days of rest. Meanwhile, Brooklyn's young guards had just taken a spin on the injury carousel. Before the game, the Nets announced that Egor Dëmin, who hasn't played in two weeks due to a bone bruise, would return tonight. However, the team also said that Nolan Traoré, who hadn't missed a game yet, would sit with right calf soreness. They also ruled out Mikel Brown Jr. due to an illness.

So, ball-handling was at a premium in the bayou. Dëmin and Danny Wolf made up the starting back court, with usual suspects Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, and Day'Ron Sharpe filling in behind them. Call it big ball. Indeed, it may have the first starting line-up ever featuring five players 6'9" or taller.

With the aforementioned injuries, Jordi Fernández didn't have many choices when putting together his starting five, but still made the right ones. With the Pelicans giving up more opponent points in the paint than anyone so far this year, beginning with the jumbo lineup made sense, and it showed on the court, with the Nets outscoring New Orleans 24-10 inside during the first period. The most they had in an opening frame all season before that was 18.

Evidenced by the above, Brooklyn's reserves got in on the action all the same. Noah Clowney, fresh off a game where he fouled out in just over seven minutes of play, knew he had to take advantage and acted accordingly, putting up six points with a block and a steal in the opening period. Wagner also added seven points, Wolf had five, and Porter Jr. led with nine. The Nets also led after one, up 39-25, giving them their largest advantage after a first quarter since April 2024.

Effective and easy-to-follow, Brooklyn had no reason to abandon its game plan in the subsequent period. The Nets got eight of their first 11 points in the second inside, and after MPJ topped that off with a three from the top of the key, Brooklyn had gone up by 17 with 7:29 to go in the second.

Holding it down from deep while everyone else went to work inside, that wasn't even Porter Jr.' best hit from downtown. With a little under four to go in the first, he also dethroned Derik Queen with this diagonal step-back…

And, knowing full well how harmful poor paint defense can be, the Nets were careful not to give up what their opponents had so frivolously surrendered. Sharpe was especially quick tonight fading back to provide extra defense around the rim, even as Zion Williamson continued to try and rummage his way in. New Orleans scored only twice inside in the second.

Saddiq Bey did threaten Brooklyn with another ugly end to a quarter. Hustling down after a Porter Jr. turnover offered up spacing in transition, Bey netted a triple that quickly brought it back to an 11 point game with roughly two and a half minutes left in the half.

The Nets didn't take it lightly. They responded with a 13-7 jolt that involved two threes from Terance Mann, one as a direct response to Bey's and another just before the horn. Brooklyn ended up going into the half up 83-66. It was the most points the Nets had scored a first half since putting up 91 on the Golden State Warriors in 2022. It's the third most points they've ever put up in a first half in team history.

By that point, Brooklyn's paint scoring advantage had swelled 40-24. They also carried a +9 advantage on the boards, along with five rejections.

So, after a period of complete interior dominance, that meant one thing one: it was time for Day'Ron Sharpe to begin shooting threes. No, I'm not kidding. And no, it didn't cost them the game. In fact, it had an opposite effect.

The Brooklyn big man hit two triples in the third's opening five minutes to give his team's lead a quick buff once play resumed. Sharpe also dished one to Egor Dëmin, who was only starting to find his groove at that point, but more on that later.

The Nets weren't just scoring from inside anymore. They were scoring from everywhere, and the Pelicans couldn't do so from anywhere, everywhere, all at once. Not before long, the home team had a look on their face Brooklyn knows all too well: one of discouragement. They stopped boxing out, closing out, and just seemed like they wanted out. The Pelicans only put up 15 points in the period.

And the Nets? Like Bill Murray in the mid 2000s, they were eager to play a new, more serious role. After Noah Clowney scooped and slammed a missed three from Mann, Brooklyn earned their largest lead of the game, going up 104-77 with about three and a half left in the third.

"He impacted the game," Fernández said of Clowney, who he said had things to "figure out" after the Dallas game. "You have size in him. He can guard multiple positions. He's switchable. He's been rebounding very well. And the efficiency, the taking good shots to get to the free throw line. Very happy with him, and we just got to keep taking positive steps here."

In the fourth, it got to a point where you almost wanted the Nets to cut it out, irrationally afraid they were burning through all their makes before the end of the road trip. Keon Ellis and Wagner added back-to-back threes to begin the final frame, getting the team to a 16-34 mark from deep by that point. They'd finish 20-41 from beyond the arc.

The Nets have long used fourth quarter blowouts to give their young players real game reps. Tonight, they got to do so from the other side of the scoreboard. Not long after the Ellis and Wagner threes, Dëmin added his own pair of triples, looking more comfortable on the floor than he has all season. The Nets seemed to run a number of the actions they normally reserve for MPJ, asking him to duck and dive around screens off ball before rising up for a catch-and-shoot three. Like his mentor, he did so each time with confidence…

Coming in like Mariano Rivera in a game where the Yankees were already up seven or eight runs, Dëmin added 12 points in the fourth to bring his total for the game to 22 on 5-of-8 shooting from the field and 4-of-6 shooting from deep.

"What impressed me? Nothing," Dëmin said of the team's overall performance. "I think that's what we're working on every day, and it's not a surprise for me how you we could sustain the energy and effort throughout the whole game, which we really need to do from night to night. Obviously it's hard to do, but it's nothing new about what we're trying to accomplish every single game."

Porter Jr. also finished with 22 points while shooting 7-of-14 from the field and 4-10 from three. He also dished three assists, grabbed a steal, and garnered six rebounds. Randle had 17 points, five assists, and four rebounds after shooting 6-of-16 from the field. Sharpe had 15 points, five assists, four rebounds, and four blocks, shooting 5-of-6 from the field and 2-of-3 from deep.

Off the bench, both Wagner and Clowney had 16 points each. Wagner added four assists while shooting 6-of=8 from the field. Clowney shot 5-of-7 from the field and 2-of-3 from three, also grabbing two steals, a block, and three rebounds. Ellis had 11 points, four rebounds, three assists, and a steal. Wolf reached 10 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, and two blocks.

"We've been practicing very well and working very well, and it's good to see that you play how you practice," Fernández said. "So, happy for the group, proud of the guys. I mean, you see everybody. Mike was composed the whole time and talked to his teammates. Julius is +38 in 29 minutes. Egor huge minutes. Mo scoring. Terrence two huge winning plays. Everybody was a big part of the win."

"Just getting into our actions, getting organized, and just having some structure," Randle added. "We were all on the same page, and we've been working at it, so it's good to see."

Final: Brooklyn Nets 145, New Orleans Pelicans 111

Day'Ron Sharpe scored 15 points with four rebounds, five assists and a career-high-tying four blocks tonight in New Orleans. It is his fourth consecutive game with at least five assists, which establishes a franchise-record streak of games with 5+ AST by a center.

Julius Randle recorded a +38 plus/minus tonight in New Orleans, which tied Stephon Marbury (4/16/99 at Seattle) as the highest plus/minus by a Net in a road game in franchise history. It tied the seventh-highest in any game by a Net.

Danny Wolf recorded a career-high 11 rebounds tonight in New Orleans to go with 10 points, four assists and two blocks. It is his second double-double of the season and fourth of his career.

Six Nets scored 15+ PTS tonight at NOP: Porter Jr., Randle, Sharpe, Dëmin, Wagner and Clowney. It ties the franchise record (15th instance) and is their second such game of the season (10/27 at BOS). This is the fourth season in franchise history with multiple such games.

Brooklyn's 83 first-half points tonight vs. New Orleans were the team's most in a first half since scoring 91 on 12/21/2022 vs. Golden State. Their 39 points in the first quarter tonight at New Orleans were their most in an opening frame this season and second most in the last two seasons, trailing only their 46 points on 2/7/26 vs. Washington.

This morning, veteran NBA writer James Herbert published a story for The Ringer on our very own Net Income. In it, you can hear from Pooch, Lucas, Sean Marks, and the countless others who've gotten close with the man behind Nets Daily over the years. I encourage all of you to check it out, and throw James a follow, who is as talented of a story teller as you'll find.

Brooklyn concludes its roadtrip on Saturday evening with a bout against the Memphis Grizzlies in Grind City. At the time of writing, the Grizz are 7-3. Isn't it cool when the lottery decides to bless you instead flip you upside down, tar and feather you? This one tips off at 8:00 p.m. EST.

#2866. Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters."

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth."

#2865. Cleveland Browns news: Silencing the QB noise

Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is still new to town, so he can be excused for not understanding how things work around here when it comes to quarterbacks.

Every decision relating to the position must be questioned and defended on a daily basis. It does not matter how many names are on the infamous quarterback jersey; the mob always wants another one added to it.

Because where is the fun of simply knowing who the starter is and practicing for that week's opponent?

Monken appears to be catching on, however, as he showed during Wednesday's announcement that quarterback Deshaun Watson would be back as the starter for this week's game against the Houston Texans after missing one game with a concussion.

It is the type of standard move that NFL teams make all the time. A starter misses a game (or games) with an injury, and once healthy, they return to their former status.

Maybe the fact that Monken is trying his best to run the Browns like a real NFL team is throwing people off. After all, despite not playing well for a full game yet this season, Watson has been instrumental in helping the Browns stay relevant into November, which is a rare feat around these parts.

Why would Monken want to go away from that, especially after watching the same script play out against New Orleans only to end with a crucial loss instead of a key win?

The answer, as it has been since the start of the season, is that he never wanted to, and it was only Watson suffering a concussion that brought a conversation no one wanted to have back into the light.

Now that Monken has answered the question, the team can focus on getting ready for the Houston Texans and attempt to avoid going into the bye week on a three-game losing streak.

We have spent enough time on all this; let's get rolling with today's edition of the Daily Dawg Chow.

#2863. Charles Barkley sounds off on epic rant after comparisons of Austin Reaves to Larry Bird: ‘They’re both white. That’s it.’

Charles Barkley admits he loves Austin Reaves, but made it clear to never again compare him to NBA legend, Larry Bird.

On Wednesday night, the Hall of Famer went off on an expletive-filled rant after he saw a clip from the Pistons broadcast team, comparing Reaves to Bird after he made an impressive shot during the Lakers' 121-116 victory on Sunday night.

"I was watching the Detroit Pistons against the Lakers the other night, and some idiot, or some fool, or jackass, thought it would be appropriate to compare Austin Reaves to Larry Bird," Barkley said. "Y'all put together a team and said, 'Who does Austin Reaves remind me of?' and y'all put together a video clip of Austin Reaves."

Charles Barkley sounds off on Pistons broadcaster who compared Austin Reaves to Larry Bird on Sunday night during "Inside the NBA." X / @ESPNNBA

"I love Austin Reaves. Don't compare him to Larry Bird ever. Under no damn circumstances."

Barkley doubled down on his take and said he loves Reaves, but "Do not ever do that again."

"Yeah, they're both white. That's it. That's the only thing they have in common. Nothing else," Barkley said.

Austin Reaves celebrating after putting together a 43-point performance against the Pistons on Sunday night. Getty Images

While Barkley revealed his true feelings for Reaves, the Lakers guard was the star on Sunday.

The team has grown accustomed to Luka Dončić scoring 40+ points in a game, but as the Lakers were without the early MVP candidate, Reaves stole the spotlight.

Aside from yelling at a Pistons fan's face, Reaves put together a 43-point performance, where he was 4-for-6 from the three-point line, shot 51.9% from the field, and 11-for-11 from the free-throw line.

Austin Reaves notches a layup in Sunday's game against the Pistons. Getty Images

Aside from scoring in abundance, Reaves also had five rebounds and four assists.

Reaves is starting to develop into the player the Lakers knew he could become, and is starting to look like he was worth every penny the team gave him after he signed a four-year, $185 million contract during the offseason.

#2858. Austin Reaves suffers heel injury vs. Bucks, x-rays negative

While the Lakers took care of business in fairly convincing fashion against the Bucks on Wednesday, the one sour note that came out of it was Austin Reaves suffering an injury.

During the third quarter, Reaves went up for a dunk and landed awkwardly. After trying to run it out for a few minutes, Reaves eventually asked for a sub and went to the locker room. He was eventually ruled out for the game.

After the game, head coach JJ Redick shared a minor update, noting that X-rays were negative and they'd get imaging on his heel Thursday. Redick also said that there was no worry of an Achilles injury.

Sexton took a blow to the face and received sutures. Luka twisted his ankle on the foot of Kyle Kuzma while shooting a 3-pointer. He stayed in the game to shoot the free throw before leaving.

Redick did not seem particularly concerned about any of the injuries and said Austin was the typical Austin postgame, so early signs are positive. Fortunately, the Lakers now have their longest break so far this season to rest and heal back up.

#2851. Taylor Fritz loves the rule change being tested at the Stockholm Open this week, ‘it definitely helps’

Taylor Fritz advanced to the Stockholm Open second round after defeating British player Cameron Norrie on Wednesday.

The American star, a former US Open finalist, defeated Norrie 7-6, 6-3 in the Swedish capital.

Fritz was made to work hard for his victory, saving one set point in the first set and multiple break points at 3-3 in the second set.

The American ultimately prevailed and can now look forward to a clash with Holger Rune in the next round.

Following Wednesday's contest, Fritz was asked about a potential rule change being tested in Stockholm this week: fresh balls are being introduced every seven games, rather than the usual nine.

It would be fair to say that Fritz is happy with the change.

"I think the most effective solution [for the quality of balls] is fixing the s–– balls, but this new rule definitely helps. Like, it definitely helps," Fritz told the Tennis Master in Stockholm.

"This would have been a very, very, miserable match to play if we were not switching after seven. Because even with the seven and seven switch, the first ball change for me was brutal because of the warm-up, actually.

"You wouldn't think it, but just adding that extra warm up plus the first seven games, at the end of the first ball change, it was already like, 'Wow, I need new balls. This is getting really rough.' It's tough to play.

"So after we got past that, changing on every seven was huge, honestly. The thing is, it matters so much on the surface, and it's really tough to tell, because here the court is tearing the balls up much more than what was happening in Paris and what was happening in Basel.

"So, the balls just react differently to different courts and different weather when we're playing outside.

"So I said this before, some weeks seven and nine is actually okay. Most weeks, seven and seven is probably better, but it'll change week to week, and this is definitely one of those weeks where a quicker ball change is needed for sure."

Fritz has long been a vocal proponent for improving the quality of tennis balls used on the ATP Tour.

Fritz recently complained about the balls used at the Shanghai Masters, stating that they 'wear out so fast.'

Fritz is far from the only individual to have voiced concerns regarding the quality of tennis balls used on the Tour in recent years.

At the Rotterdam Open in February, Daniil Medvedev described the HEAD Tour XT balls as 'terrible'.

Fritz and Rune – who recently returned from a long-term injury suffered at the 2025 Stockholm Open – first played each other at the 2023 Miami Open.

Fritz came out on top against the 2022 Paris Masters champion, triumphing 6-3, 6-4 in the Round of 16.

Just under one year later, Rune avenged his Miami defeat.

The Danish youngster beat Fritz 2-6, 7-6, 6-3 in the 2024 Indian Wells Round of 16. Rune went on to lose in the quarter-finals to Daniil Medvedev.

Fritz bounced back emphatically in their third and final contest, beating Rune 6-1, 6-2 in the 2024 Shanghai Masters Round of 16.

Fritz defeated David Goffin in the quarter-finals, before losing to Novak Djokovic in the last four.

#2849. Fantasy football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: 30 players to start or sit in Week 10

The 2026 NFL trade deadline passed ahead of Week 10, shaking things up for some fantasy managers as they look to make critical start- 'em, sit- 'em decisions.

The most notable trade involved the Minnesota Vikings acquiring quarterback Kirk Cousins to serve as an upgrade for their offense. Cousins' presence should raise the ceiling for players like Justin Jefferson, while his departure from the Las Vegas Raiders will raise questions about the viability of players like Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty.

Elsewhere, Jonathan Taylor remained with the Indianapolis Colts, dumping cold water on those who had been holding out in hopes of a trade that would turn Seth McGowan into the team's lead back. And fantasy managers will have to continue dealing with bye weeks that are knocking out the likes of Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift, Bucky Irving and Saquon Barkley.

JUSTIN JEFFERSON: Kirk Cousins trade is good news for Vikings WR

Who can you start and sit in fantasy football for Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season? USA TODAY Sports outlines 30 players to trust or fade this week:

Jared Goff, Detroit Lions (vs. New England Patriots)

There may be temptation to sit Goff after he failed to throw a touchdown pass last week against the Dolphins, but he has a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Patriots. New England has allowed a league-high 2,256 passing yards to quarterbacks this season and just struggled to contain speed threats Christian Watson and Matthew Golden in Week 9. Goff should be able to hit some chunk plays with his talented receiving corps.

Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams (at Arizona Cardinals)

Similar to Goff, Stafford has had a couple of quiet games in a row, posting just one passing touchdown in each of his last two outings. He should be better equipped for a big-time game against the Cardinals, who have allowed the second-most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to quarterbacks this season, and against whom Stafford has thrown multiple touchdowns in three consecutive games.

Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers (at New Orleans Saints)

After a couple of down games, Young enjoyed a strong showing against a Broncos defense that is adept at pressuring the quarterback, inspiring confidence he will continue to be a solid starter even in less-favorable matchups. The Saints have allowed the 11th-most FPPG to quarterbacks this season and Young should have plenty of opportunities to hit downfield shots off play action.

Audric Estime, New Orleans Saints (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Three teams have allowed at least 11 rushing touchdowns to running backs this season. The Panthers are one of them and they have surrendered at least one rushing touchdown in five consecutive games. Estime took over as the between-the-tackles leader for the Saints last week after Kendre Miller's release, so he can be trusted as a flex with touchdown upside – provided Travis Etienne Jr. remains out of the lineup.

Ollie Gordon II, Miami Dolphins (at Indianapolis Colts)

Gordon has cooled slightly after four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, but he gets a nice matchup against the Colts in Week 10. Indianapolis has allowed the fourth-most FPPG to running backs this season and is one of four teams to allow 1,000 rushing yards.

Jadarian Price, Seattle Seahawks (at Las Vegas Raiders)

Zach Charbonnet figures to see more between-the-carries opportunities than Price, but the first-round rookie still saw nine carries and caught four passes for 54 yards against the Cardinals. His touch floor looks fairly solid, so he should be able to do damage against a Raiders defense that has allowed the third-most FPPG to running backs this season.

Corey Kiner, New England Patriots (vs. Detroit Lions)

Kiner looks poised to become New England's backfield leader with Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined. The 24-year-old has averaged 4.9 yards per carry and his high-volume status should be enough to make him a quality flex play even against a Lions defense that has thrived against the run.

Jameson Williams, Detroit Lions (vs. New England Patriots)

The Patriots just surrendered a combined 17 receptions, 335 receiving yards and two touchdowns to the speedy duo of Watson and Golden in Week 9. Williams should be well-positioned to use his speed to get deep against a New England defense that has allowed the most FPPG to receivers this season.

KC Concepcion, Cleveland Browns (vs. Houston Texans)

The Texans figure to pressure Deshaun Watson often in Week 10, just as they did Justin Herbert in Week 9, but Houston is still susceptible to allowing big plays to receivers. They just surrendered catches of 58 and 50 yards to Quentin Johnston and KeAndre Lambert-Smith respectively last week and have allowed the second-most FPPG to receivers this season. Concepcion could similarly rip off some chunk plays thanks to his speed and elusiveness.

Deebo Samuel, San Francisco 49ers (at Dallas Cowboys)

Samuel returned to 49ers practice on Wednesday and may have a chance to suit up against the Cowboys. If he does, feel free to fire him up as a flex play against a Cowboys defense that has allowed the seventh-most FPPG to receivers this season.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (vs. San Francisco 49ers)

Flournoy has averaged 3.8 receptions and 58.2 receiving yards over his last five games while establishing himself as the clear-cut No. 3 target in Dallas' offense. The Cowboys will likely have to throw a lot to keep their matchup with the 49ers close, so Flournoy could emerge as a high-upside flex, especially if George Pickens is limited in any fashion after missing last week with a hamstring injury.

Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (vs. New Orleans Saints)

Waller hasn't been consistent this season, but he remains an imposing receiving threat, as he showed in Week 9, racking up eight catches for 90 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos. The 34-year-old gets another favorable matchup against a Saints defense that has allowed the sixth-most FPPG to TEs this year, so he should threaten to score again in Week 10.

Hunter Henry, New England Patriots (vs. Detroit Lions)

The Lions have been better against tight ends lately, but they have still given up a league-high 704 receiving yards and 11 receiving touchdowns to the position. That should give Henry a chance to emerge as a potential top-five play at tight end this week.

Baltimore Ravens (vs. Los Angeles Chargers)

There are precious few defenses that can't be started against the Chargers. Herbert has been sacked 31 times in eight games this season and has thrown at least one interception across those contests, making Jesse Minter's stop unit a high-floor play.

The Bills just put together an elite defensive performance against the Vikings, intercepting Carson Wentz three times and holding Minnesota to six points. Geno Smith and the Jets may be live to perform a bit better, but the Bills should still be able to do enough to emerge as a top-10 fantasy defense this week.

Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

Love has been one of the league's most consistent quarterbacks this season and threw for 387 yards and two touchdowns against the Vikings in Week 1. Still, trusting him against a Minnesota defense that ranks No. 1 overall in pressure rate, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats, and has surrendered the fewest FPPG to quarterbacks seems like a risky proposition.

Fernando Mendoza, Las Vegas Raiders (vs. Seattle Seahawks)

It will be fun to see Mendoza make his first NFL start after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, but don't expect the Indiana product to have a great outing. The Seahawks are allowing just one passing touchdown per game to quarterbacks this season, so Mendoza has a low floor/ceiling combination in this matchup.

Drew Lock, Seattle Seahawks (at Las Vegas Raiders)

Lock has a solid matchup against the Raiders, but trusting him is risky. Seattle's backup quarterback is dealing with a nagging oblique injury, which could lead the Seahawks to lean more on their running game. The Seahawks may also be able to build a big lead if they can stymie Mendoza, so Lock may not have to throw too much in this matchup.

Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans (vs. Jacksonville Jaguars)

Pollard posted 246 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns across his two games leading into the Titans' bye, so it's hard to recommend sitting him. Still, the Jaguars are allowing just 89.3 rushing yards per game, fifth-best in the league, so the veteran's upside is limited in an unfavorable matchup.

Tyler Allgeier, Arizona Cardinals (vs. Los Angeles Rams)

Allgeier handled almost all of Arizona's running back work with Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight out in Week 9, but he turned it into just 46 yards on 19 touches. Allgeier should continue to have a sizable workload in the Cardinals' backfield rotation, but he is too touchdown-dependent to trust against a Rams defense that has surrendered just three total touchdowns to the position.

Quinshon Judkins, Cleveland Browns (vs. Houston Texans)

The Texans are an odd defense in that they are allowing 103 rushing yards per game, which ranks 13th in the league, but they have only surrendered rushing touchdowns in three of their eight games. Granted, those touchdowns have come in waves, but it nonetheless bodes well for their chances of stopping Judkins, who has averaged just 3.3 yards per carry this season, rendering him a touchdown-dependent fantasy option.

Kaleb Johnson, Green Bay Packers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

The Packers are without Josh Jacobs, which would ostensibly push Johnson into the team's lead running back role. That said, Green Bay has averaged a league-worst 68.2 rushing yards per game, so trusting Johnson against an elite Vikings defense doesn't seem like a great gamble.

Tank Dell, Houston Texans (at Cleveland Browns)

Dell posted four catches for 105 yards and a touchdown on a team-high nine targets and saw his snap share increase to 47.1% in the Texans' Week 9 win over the Chargers. Will he continue to get that type of snap split and target share? If so, he will become a weekly starter because of his deep playmaking capabilities. Still, we'll need more than a one-game sample size to trust him against a Browns defense that has been solid against receivers this season.

DK Metcalf, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Cincinnati Bengals)

The Steelers may have to throw a lot to beat the Bengals, but will that guarantee a big game for Metcalf? He has posted three or fewer catches in three of his last four outings and is catching a career-low 51.6% of his passes. That makes him hard to trust even in what could be a higher-scoring game.

Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins (at Indianapolis Colts)

The Colts have struggled this season, but they still have a good cornerback duo of Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward. That will make it hard for Dolphins backup quarterback Kyle McCord to consistently get the ball to Douglas.

Adonai Mitchell, New York Jets (vs. Buffalo Bills)

Game script could help Mitchell rack up targets against the Bills, but it's hard to recommend trusting him after he was shut out in two of his last three games. The presence of Omar Cooper Jr. and the pending return of Garrett Wilson will only continue to erode his ceiling.

Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

Love has focused heavily on targeting Watson and Golden this season, leaving Kraft as the offense's tertiary option. He has still posted strong outings most weeks, but he will be hard-pressed to do that in Week 10 against a Vikings defense that has been far and away the best against tight ends this season.

T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings (at Green Bay Packers)

Hockenson's outlook should improve with Cousins joining the fold, but the impact might not be immediate. The Packers have allowed the fourth-fewest FPPG to tight ends this season, so this is probably a stay-away spot for the veteran.

New Orleans Saints (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Some may look at Bryce Young's recent numbers (14 sacks, four interceptions over his last three games) as a reason to back the Saints in this spot. However, Young just threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns against a strong Denver Broncos defense, so he could be in for a good outing against a porous Saints stop unit.

There may be temptation to start the Colts against Miami's McCord-ed offense, but it's hard to trust an Indianapolis team that has struggled to generate consistent pressure to deliver, even in a favorable matchup.

#2848. Diving deeper into Cavs 115-107 win over Knicks: James Harden showed why he’s integral to Cleveland’s success

For one night, the Cleveland Cavaliers exorcised their demons at Madison Square Garden. They came away with an impressive 115-107 win over the defending champion New York Knicks.

32 points on 9-for-14 shooting, 4 assists, 2 rebounds, 2 steals

Few players in NBA history have been able to single-handedly raise an offense's floor and ceiling like Harden. His ability to score from anywhere, manipulate defenders with his body, and make every pass made him nearly unguardable in his prime — while also allowing him to remain effective into his late 30s. However, that offensive consistency hasn't been there yet for the Cavs at the start of the season.

Harden needs his scoring and playmaking to work in concert with each other if he's going to elevate an offense. When he's scoring well, he draws the attention of the entire defense, which leaves teammates open for easy shots. But when he isn't able to create space off the dribble or connect on the outside shot, defenders can stay home with their assignments. And when they are staying home, those openings for Harden to set up teammates just aren't there. Everything is based on his scoring.

Over the last handful of games, we saw just how bad things can look when Harden isn't scoring. Defenses don't have to respect him and send multiple players his way. Things then become stagnant, and the entire offense suffers because of it. Against the Knicks, we witnessed the inverse.

The difference in this one was shotmaking. Harden found a scoring rhythm in the second quarter with his outside shot. This caused his defender to guard him much closer on the perimeter, making it easier for him to get inside the paint. The Knicks chose not to send multiple defenders his way, which allowed him to continue his effective scoring and close this game out with nine clutch fourth-quarter points.

It's not too much of a stretch to say that the success of the entire team depends on Harden. Everything offensively rises and falls with his play. The Cavs need to see this version of Harden much more often than they have.

21 points on 7-of-11 shoooting, 11 rebounds, 8 assists

Towns is playing the best basketball of his career. His unique skill set allows him to affect the game in so many different ways. He proved that again here with his outside shooting, playmaking, and rebounding.

The Cavs bigs tried to contain Towns — his offense was just better than their defense.

23 points on 8-of-15 shooting, 7 rebounds, 6 assists, 2 steals

Mitchell provided timely scoring while also being a good decision-maker. He correctly got the ball out of his hands and to his teammates when New York threw doubles at him. And his teammates rewarded him for doing so with the win.

Cleveland also did much better at controlling the glass. Head coach Kenny Atkinson has talked about rebounding being something everyone on the court needs to be involved in. Mitchell chipping in went a long way in making sure rebounding wasn't an issue.

Anything bought from the links helps support Fear the Sword. You can also shop all of Homage's Cavs gear HERE. The link to the Donovan Mitchell NBA Jam shirt is HERE.

Combined stats: 22 points on 7-of-20 shooting, 10 rebounds, 7 assists

The Knicks' incredible championship run was partially fueled by phenomenal play from their three starting wings. Likewise, their inability to show up to this game is a big reason why the Cavs were able to come away with a win.

Anunoby was helpful defensively, but couldn't find the range from the field, going 3-for-9. Bridges played just 17 minutes and was benched down the stretch due to being a complete non-factor. And Hart couldn't find his shot and wasn't an impactful rebounder.

Swing players often decide games against two high-powered teams like this. In this contest, New York's supporting pieces just didn't show up.

14 points on 6-of-11 shooting, 4 rebounds, 2 steals, 1 assist

We've yet to encounter a moment that was too big for Thomas. He played with a confidence that's rare to see in a rookie making his debut at MSG against the defending champions.

Thomas is first and foremost a scorer. We saw that again as he was able to create off the dribble and knock down open threes when the ball swung to him on the perimeter.

Atkinson has been able to continue putting Thomas in the rotation because of how he can positively influence the game in areas besides scoring. Defensively, he did a good job of guarding his man, didn't get lost off-ball, and forced two steals. Thomas was also effective at attacking the offensive glass as he came away with three offensive rebounds.

Thomas is scoring, but he's also doing a lot of the little things right that you need to in order to be a rotation player. This was another good outing for a rookie who has made nights like this feel routine.

15 points on 6-of-12 shooting, 3 rebounds, 1 assist

Proctor showed the wide array of skills that he has. He initiated the offense as a secondary ball-handler, knocked down outside shots when the ball swung to him, and was helpful defensively.

This was exactly what you want to see from someone who's trying to prove that he should stay in the rotation when Sam Merril and Nae'Qwan Tomlin return from injury.

7 points on 2-of-12 shooting, 5 rebounds, 4 blocks, 4 assists

Watson's defensive effort made up for his poor shooting. He was seemingly everywhere on defense and secured the victory with a chase-down block on Deuce McBride.

The Knicks only got 24.4% of their missed shots (21st percentile) while the Cavs grabbed 32.6% of available offensive rebounds (65th percentile).

The Cavs controlled the glass, won the possession battle, and ultimately won the game.

This game doesn't fix all that has been wrong with the Cavaliers at the start of the season. Nor does it show that they're going to put the pieces together and become the team they have the potential to be. It does, however, demonstrate that the Cavs have the talent to beat anyone.

The Cavs were impressive on both ends of the floor. Offensively, their two elite guards controlled the game while still making way for role players like Proctor and Thomas to make meaningful contributions.

Defensively, Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley made it difficult to score inside and kept the Knicks off the free-throw line. Watson also made a sizeable impact as a point-of-attack defender and weak-side rim protector. This resulted in New York becoming more of an outside-shooting team than they would've liked.

In short, this was a complete performance.

The Cavs have had other impressive wins this season, but they haven't been able to back any of them up with anything substantive. At this point, we don't know what team we'll see on a nightly basis, and there's no evidence that they're creating sustainable habits that will help them in the postseason. This win will only be different if they can actually build off it from a process and results standpoint.

#2846. ‘I’m hoping’ – Patrick Mahomes admits his wife may not love his pregnancy plans

Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, shared the news earlier this week that they are expecting their fourth child next year.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback is in the middle of the 2026 NFL season and is pushing the Chiefs towards a spot in the postseason. However, the focus remains on making it to the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium in February.

Last year was a stressful one for the Mahomes family after the 31-year-old quarterback suffered a season-ending injury in December. "I'm hoping. I'm hoping. I don't know if Brittany is, but I'm hoping. If we can keep that going and get another Super Bowl win with a baby on the way, that would be awesome, for sure," Mahomes replied during Wednesday's press conference.

"It's a blessing to have another baby on the way. I'm excited for it. I'm hoping that me and Bronze can even up the score, but I'm just praying for a healthy baby at the end of the day."

The Chiefs have got their eyes set on the Super Bowl in February, but they will need to clean up their game slightly following their recent losses to the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos. They were able to add wide receiver Josh Downs to the roster in an attempt to boost Mahomes' offense.

With teams like the Cincinnati Bengals heating up and the Buffalo Bills looking seriously competitive, the Chiefs are going to have to be at their absolute best for Mahomes to get his wish of making it to another Super Bowl.

#2843. George Russell takes major step outside F1 with ambitious new project

George Russell has announced the launch of his own karting academy, an initiative designed to identify promising young drivers and help them overcome the financial barriers that often prevent talented youngsters from progressing in motorsport.

The Mercedes driver unveiled the GR63 Academy on Thursday, 12 November, through his official Instagram account. The programme will be run in partnership with Silverstone and the British Racing Drivers' Club (BRDC), with 25 children set to receive places in its inaugural season in 2027.

Russell hopes the initiative will give aspiring racing drivers an opportunity to develop their abilities, particularly those who might otherwise struggle to secure the financial support needed to pursue their ambitions.

Announcing the project on social media, Russell reflected on the importance of karting in his own journey towards Formula 1 and explained why he wants to help the next generation of drivers.

"So proud to introduce you all to the GR63 Academy. Karting is where it all started for me and has played a crucial role in my career," the Briton wrote.

"I also know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight."

Russell made clear that his ambition goes beyond simply identifying young drivers with potential. He also wants to ensure they receive the assistance and guidance necessary to take the next steps in their careers.

"With the GR63 Academy, I want to give something back to my sport by finding those hidden stars and giving them the support and guidance they need to reach their potential."

The selection process will take place at Silverstone, beginning with qualifying sessions in December 2026. The initial stage will cost £25 to enter, with the most promising participants progressing to a further selection round in January 2027.

The academy will ultimately select 25 young drivers to compete in a fully funded eight-round championship between March and November 2027.

At the end of the season, the five leading competitors will progress to a final assessment, with the successful driver earning a fully funded karting campaign in 2028.

Russell also confirmed his involvement in selecting the participants, explaining how the first stages of the programme will determine who earns a place: "Following the first two rounds at Silverstone, I'll identify 25 kids to take part in the GR63 Academy in 2027."

#2841. Nets' Noah Clowney and Pelicans' Julian Reese get into on-court altercation, 4 technical fouls issued

The Brooklyn Nets were leading the New Orleans Pelicans by 38 with less than five minutes left on Wednesday. That didn't stop tensions from boiling over.

Nets big man Noah Clowney and Pelicans forward Julian Reese got into an altercation that began with Clowney falling to the floor while jostling for a free-throw rebound and ended with a full scrum formed around the baseline. Replay showed Reese giving Clowney a shove and Clowney grabbing Reese's arm as he went down.

The two got face-to-face once Clowney got up, with teammates and officials intervening to break up the confrontation.

The play was ruled a loose-ball foul by Reese with offsetting technical fouls for Reese, Clowney, Pelicans guard Jaron Pierre Jr. and Nets wing Terance Mann. The Nets won 145-111.

The incident is the latest in a series of altercations for Clowney, whom the Nets selected 21st overall out of Alabama in the 2023 NBA Draft but have declined to extend up to now. There was his run-in with Dallas Mavericks rookie Morez Johnson last weekend.

There was his exchange with Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson last month.

And in February, he had quite the sequence with Rui Hachimura, then of the Los Angeles Lakers.

Clowney entered Wednesday averaging 19.7 minutes in 10 games, his lowest average since his rookie season. He was also posting a career-low 5.0 points per game.

#2840. Best available free agent edge rushers for Bengals to target after failed Arnold Ebiketie trade

The Cincinnati Bengals rarely make a trade at the deadline, which is why it was somewhat surprising that a trade was reported on Tuesday when they (briefly) acquired Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles.

However, the trade seems to have dissolved behind the scenes after the team realized the deal would also cost them a third-round compensatory pick they are hoping to receive from Trey Hendrickson signing with the Ravens. Then, for the rest of the deadline, no more moves were made, although it is unknown if any more trades were attempted or if they elected to stand pat once the Ebiketie deal fell through.

The attempted trade for Ebiketie, though, is a clear indicator that the Bengals are not happy with the depth of their defensive end room. Cashius Howell is on IR for an unknown amount of time, and Shemar Stewart is getting few snaps and was even a healthy inactive for a game.

With all of that, the failed trade, and no more trade possibilities, the Bengals could target the position through one of the free agents still available on the market, so let's take a look at the top available defensive ends.

The 31-year-old Bosa was one of the top edge rushers in the NFL for most of his career; he last played in Buffalo in 2025 on a one-year, $12 million deal. In the offseason, he was in the discussion for many fanbases, but no rumored meetings or potential signings popped up, and in the summer it was hinted he may have even quietly retired, with Adam Schefter saying he may have played his final snap.

However, in the last month there has been more buzz about him possibly coming back and joining a team for a run to the Super Bowl, mainly his previous team, the Bills, or joining his brother Nick Bosa in San Francisco.

It is not impossible to imagine, though, a world where he wants to join his close friend Joe Burrow in Cincinnati for a title run as well, and the Bengals should not hesitate to call and see if it is possible.

The 34-year-old Floyd is another older pass rusher who was productive relatively recently, now getting a lot of buzz as a potential addition for teams looking to make a Super Bowl push. On a one-year, $10 million deal in 2025, Floyd had a decent year and can still get involved as a pass rusher.

The Bengals should be a desirable destination for any free agent edge rushers with their talented offense and impactful interior, giving edge rushers a lot of one-on-one matchups in obvious passing situations. As a rotational pass rusher, Floyd would fit exactly what the Bengals need.

The 32-year-old Reddick was one of the best pass rushers in the league for several years and was a double-digit sack player with Philadelphia. His production in recent years has really taken a nosedive, but the Bengals could sign him with the hope that he has fresh legs, not playing most of the year, and could be effectively deployed in a limited capacity to keep him fresh.

If Reddick could find something even close to his 2023 form, he could be extremely impactful.

The youngest player on the list by a long shot, 28-year-old Yetur Gross-Matos signed a two-year deal with the 49ers in free agency in 2024. During that contract, though, he missed roughly half of his games with the team and wasn't a consistent performer in the games he did play in.

Gross-Matos did have flashes, and with him now either healthy or very close to it after a knee injury last year, he could be one of the more intriguing options, since he is still young and could have several years of impactful football ahead of him.

The Bengals have quite a few options available if they want some fresh legs and some help in the pass-rushing department. If they were willing to spend a sixth-round pick, they should be more than willing to spend a few million dollars if it is the difference-maker in getting the Super Bowl win.

#2836. Nets pound Pelicans for much-needed bounceback win

NEW ORLEANS — The Nets came to New Orleans desperate for a bounce-back win. And they made it look easy in the Big Easy.

What Brooklyn got was a bounce-back beating, pounding the pitiful Pelicans 145-111 before 15,043 at Smoothie King Center on Wednesday night.

In a matchup of slumping teams coming off humbling losses, the Nets were the ones who showed some steel.

They lost to the Mavericks by 37, while the Pelicans were stinging from the worst regular-season defeat in their history, a 51-point humiliation to Golden State.

Moritz Wagner (13) celebrates after making a basket during the Nets' 145-111 blowout win over the Pelicans on Nov. 11, 2026, in New Orleans. AP Photo/Tyler Kaufman

On Wednesday, a Brooklyn team that looked in disarray in Dallas put up their highest-scoring first half in years, led by as many as 41 points and welcomed back Egor Dëmin with a resounding rout.

It was a rare laugher for the Nets (3-8), a complete team victory. Even without point guards Nolan Traore and Mikel Brown Jr., the Nets handed out 30 assists to just 15 turnovers. They shot 57 percent and 20 of 41 from deep.

And Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle looked like the veteran leaders they're being paid to be. Not because they were good, but because they made others better.

The former had a team-high tying 22 points, while the latter was a plus-38, tying Stephon Marbury for the best in franchise history for a road game.

"I just told Ju, me and him [are] going to have to take it on ourselves to get us organized and be in the right place, be involved in the offense," Porter said. "So we were just trying to communicate more, make quicker decisions and get into things quicker."

"We've got a lot of capable guys. I don't know how many people are in double figures. It seemed like a lot, though. So we got capable dudes. And when we share the ball like that, everyone gets to have fun, feel like they're in a rhythm. We can be pretty good offensively."

It was eight in double figures, but six with at least 15 points — Dëmin, Porter Jr., Randle, Day'Ron Sharpe and backups Moritz Wagner and Noah Clowney — to tie a franchise record.

For a bench that has struggled, that kind of balance was key.

Julius Randle drives to the basket during the Nets' blowout win over the Pelicans. NBAE via Getty Images

Brooklyn came out of the blocks quickly, with Danny Wolf — who had another double-double — giving them a 12-5 lead.

It was 39-25 by the end of the opening period, their second-highest scoring first quarter of the last two years. It got better in the second half.

For much of the early part of this season, the Nets bench has struggled. On Wednesday night, they didn't just hold their own, but were additive. And that's even without their pair of 20-year-old point guards.

Wagner had seven points in the first quarter and 13 by the break.

He had a ferocious dunk on Jordan Poole for an and-one that put the Nets up 31-19, and followed with a nice drive and a flex afterward.

Brooklyn took an 83-66 cushion into intermission when Randle found Terance Mann for a last-second 3. It was their highest-scoring half since Dec. 21, 2022 (when they had 91 against Golden State).

Danny Wolf rises up for a layup during the Nets' blowout win over the Pelicans. NBAE via Getty Images

"We executed really well offensively in the first half, and when everybody touches the ball, everybody sees the ball go through the net, it's a lot more fun. You play with a lot of effort," Wagner said. "We've got to find a way to do it in games where the ball doesn't go through the rim as much, but of course that was an 80-point half and I think that was a lot of fun for everybody."

It became an outright laugher in the second.

A putback dunk by Noah Clowney (who had a bounce-back 16-point night) padded it to 104-77 with 3:36 left in the third.

And unlike Atlanta to start this trip — when they blew a 17-point lead and fell to the Hawks — this time the Nets actually built on it, padding it to 41.

"We've got to bring the same energy, same focus to every game," Sharpe said. "No matter the score, no matter what's happening, no matter who's out, we all got to approach the game the same way."

#2835. Commanders look to stay alive against Giants in 'TNF' game Jayden Daniels called 'must win'

Fueled by defeat, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was not shy about labeling his team's next game.

"Must win," Daniels told reporters after the Commanders' 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.

That date with destiny has arrived 96 hours later, with his team facing the New York Giants on "Thursday Night Football" Nov. 12 (8:15 p.m. ET, Amazon Prime Video). But head coach Dan Quinn, facing job-security questions with his team sitting at 2-5-1 and heading into a mini-bye, does not see the game in the same light.

"For me … I try to avoid the declarations of that. I've been around the league long enough to know that lots of season to play and lots of football to go," Quinn said.

Not afraid to speak for everybody in the organization in this instance, Quinn offered a different way to categorize it.

"We need this and we're battling for it," Quinn said. "That's really where the focus is, but we don't get into the big declaration stuff."

During the Week 5 meeting between the two teams, it was the lack of an outcome – the two teams played the lone tie in the NFL this season – that seemed to doom the Commanders' season. Daniels and the offense mismanaged the clock with no timeouts remaining in the final minute of overtime, and the clock expired before the team could kick the game-winning field goal.

"We know that the Giants," Daniels said this week. "They have a lot of good athletic players out there that they like to get into the mix and blitz, you know, try to create mismatch and matchups and stuff like that. So, we just gotta prepare for that and then really adjust from there on out."

Now another prime-time matchup against a division rival presents an additional high-profile assignment in a season defined by bad optics. The following week, on "Monday Night Football" against the San Francisco 49ers, the Commanders once again appeared confused – this time about what down it was – when Daniels threw the ball away on fourth down. Quinn's reaction did not assuage the critics of his game management. Neither did the call on the final play of the Rams' loss when the ball did not reach the end zone despite trailing by a touchdown.

A win against the Giants would move Washington two games back in the loss column and keep the Commanders alive in the NFC East race, with the Giants using backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who enters the matchup nursing a hip pointer that limited him last Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Part of the Commanders' slow start is tied to Quinn's two first-year coordinators, David Blough (offense) and Daronte Jones (defense). Quinn shot down speculation that he could make staff changes with another loss. Then there is the question of Quinn's own job security, especially if the Commanders find themselves.

"I'd say we're all frustrated," Quinn said.

What encouraged Quinn during practice this week was the offense having zero incompletions prior to the game and executing during the situational periods – red zone and third down. Washington ranks 23rd in red-zone touchdown drives and last in third-down conversion rate. Luckily for the Commanders, the Giants are last in red-zone defense, allowing a touchdown on nearly four out of every five drives that reach their 20-yard line (78.95%).

"He's still growing as a coordinator, first-time coordinator, still going through his growing pains and stuff like that," Daniels said of Blough. "So, I just try to do the best I can, just go out there, execute, doesn't matter what the play call is, it doesn't matter anything. If we got all 11 people going in the same direction, we have a chance."

#2833. Player Grades: Lakers vs. Bucks

The start of this game had all the makings of a game in Milwaukee amidst a November road trip.

The Lakers entered the game with Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain) being the only player unavailable but left it with Luka Dončić rolling his ankle, Austin Reaves tweaking his left heel and Collin Sexton bloodied after an incidental headbutt with Ryan Rollins.

Despite the start and the injuries, Los Angeles took care of business and carries a six-game win streak into Phoenix to close out its first extended road trip of the season.

So, let's dive into the win. As always, grades are based on expectations for each player. A "B" grade represents the average performance for that player.

21 minutes, 0 points, 9 rebounds, 6 assists, 0-4 FG, +14

The box score didn't treat LaRavia the best this game, but his impact continues to defy counting stats. Fifty-fifty balls, defense, running in transition, all factors in the Lakers being a plus-14 while LaRavia was on the floor.

29 minutes, 10 points, 11 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 block, 1 steal, 4 fouls, 5-10 FG, +19

I thought Kessler started this game a bit too passive around the rim defensively and it set the tone for the rest of his game. Nonetheless, he was yet again a crucial conduit between the Lakers' defensive and offensive production.

23 minutes, 8 points, 5 rebounds, 3 steals, 2 turnovers, 3-6 FG, 2-4 3PT, +4

It took Thybulle a half to really make his impact felt, but he continues to be a steady producer on both sides of the ball. Steals, deflections and threes have defined his impact this season and it was the same tonight.

32 minutes, 32 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists, 5 turnovers, 3 steals, 10-25 FG, 5-12 3PT, 7-10 FT, +21

Luka makes it nine straight 30-point games but tweaked his ankle with around four minutes left in the game and the Lakers up by 20. Dončić was good, again, but started this game with a questionable shot diet and committed some lousy turnovers.

Of course you take the good with the bad, but Dončić's start of the game held him back from this being another all-around great game.

25 minutes, 18 points, 5 assists, 3 rebounds, 3 steals, 1 turnover, 6-10 FG, 1-3 3PT, 5-5 FT, +23

Before leaving the game with his injury, Reaves was the ying to Dončić's yang, providing the Lakers with balance, a steady shot diet and conservative ball handling. If it weren't for the injury, Reaves was well on his way to yet another efficient 20-plus-point outing.

26 minutes, 23 points, 3 rebounds, 2 assists, 9-15 FG, 5-8 3PT, +21

Mamu is stringing together some of the best games of his Lakers tenure. His connectivity was on full display tonight, draining threes and seemingly switching onto everyone on defense. His ability to relieve stress both in transition and in the half-court on offense remains invaluable.

Should Reaves or Dončić miss time, having someone like Mamu is a luxury.

20 minutes, 9 points, 5 assists, 2 steals, 4-5 FG, 1-1 3PT, +11

Speaking of continued production, Williams remained a consistent bench player tonight. His defensive intensity, especially on Tyler Herro leading to a scuffle, is an important aspect in keeping an otherwise below-average group above water. It also helps when he makes his threes.

13 minutes, 10 points, 3 assists, 1 rebound, 1 turnover, 1 steal, 4-8 FG, 0-3 3PT, 2-2 FT, +1

It's been an up-and-down season for Sexton thus far, but he continues to show improved poise when handling the ball in the non-Luka minutes. However, it still feels like he takes up a little too much of the usage when sharing the floor with Reaves.

13 minutes, 0 points, 2 rebounds, 2 turnovers, 0-3 3PT, -13

This road trip was good for the rookie, who got some real minutes in a couple of games. Tonight was evidence that Carr is still getting his footing and adjusting to the pace of the game. Aside from diving on the floor for a ball he lost, I feel we're still yet to really see how much of an impact he can have on the floor.

Vando played just nine minutes, but each of them was impactful. He brought instant energy in his first shift and continues to show improved aggression around the rim. He's had four points.

James, Hardy and Looney each played four minutes of garbage time after Dončić rolled his ankle and, yet again, almost blew a lead. Each of them was a minus-13 in their shift. Hardy has the greenest light in the NBA, James remains passive and susceptible to pressure and Looney took the floor for the first time in weeks (give him some grace).

Redick admitted that tonight could have easily been a trap game given how the team started. Many will also dock him for keeping Dončić in the game with four minutes left while up 20 when he eventually tweaked his ankle, but his explanation that the star wouldn't have been out there if Sexton didn't go down was reasonable.

The Lakers are on a seven-game win streak and Redick is pushing all the right buttons.

#2829. Sean McVay laughs as he says he's tempted to ask assistant coach Robert Woods to suit up

He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries.

McVay was asked during his press conference whether he has talked to the 34-year-old Woods, who was a receiver for the Rams for five years, about potentially playing again.

"I have, yes," McVay answered with a laugh.

McVay acknowledged that there are Collective Bargaining Agreement rules against a coach becoming a player, but he said Woods is still in great shape and it would be fun to give it a try.

"I've looked at him, and the way he looks out there, I've definitely been tempted," McVay said. "I think that'd be a violation of the CBA. I don't know what he'd have to do, but he looks damn good and still is smooth out there. Very tempting."

Woods was cut by the Steelers before the 2025 season and hasn't played since, and he announced his retirement and signed a one-day contract with the Rams in February of 2026. Realistically, even with his intimate knowledge of the Rams' offense, he probably wouldn't be able to contribute as much on the field as whatever receiver the Rams could add off waivers or another team's practice squad.

If Woods and the Rams actually wanted him to become an active player, it wouldn't be as simple as signing him to the active roster, as the league has rules preventing that. Players on the reserve-retired list have to pass through waivers before they can join a team. And the NFL generally doesn't allow coaches to become players: In 2020, when the Broncos lost all their quarterbacks to covid, they asked the league office if they could activate one of their assistant coaches and were told no. In 2009, Eagles coach Andy Reid wanted to play coaching intern Matt Nagy at quarterback in a preseason game and was also told by the league that he couldn't.

So the idea of Woods playing receiver for the Rams is probably not going to get any kind of serious consideration. Even if, with all the Rams' injuries, it's tempting.

#2828. Rapid Recap: Lakers 123, Bucks 112

The Milwaukee Bucks put up an early fight against the Los Angeles Lakers but ultimately fell short, losing 123-112. Tyler Herro led all Bucks scorers with 27 points and seven assists, while Jaime Jaquez Jr.—coming off the bench for the first time this year—dropped 25 points. Luka Doncic led the Lakers with 30 points, while Sandro Mamukelashvili led the Lakers' second unit with 23 off the bench.

Earlier in the day, it was announced that Myles Turner would rest, Kel'el Ware would start, Nate Ament would start at SF, and Tyler Herro would be available. That lineup got off to a hot start, with Herro hitting a mid-range floater before Brayden Burries showed incredible body control, scoring over Walker Kessler with a tricky little finger roll. Of course, Luka Doncic needed just four minutes to score nine points—and he hardly broke a sweat—as the Lakers pulled out a 14-7 lead. Jenkins began rotating through the bench early, and tried several lineups and looks that kept LA on their toes. One of these rotations was Jaime Jaquez Jr., who seemed to have a respawn point under the hoop and, almost at Luka speed, scored eight points to keep the game within one possession for the rest of the first. Bucks down 30-28 after one.

Milwaukee stayed aggressive on defense to open the second, which helped keep the Lakers within striking distance. After LA built their lead back to eight, came the highlight of the night: Nate Ament posterizing Kessler on the fast break to snap the cold streak. Whew. Jaquez continued his effective play, matching Herro through the middle of the second with 13 points to lead the team in scoring. However, Milwaukee then hit their usual cold stretch, allowing the Lakers to piece together a 7-0 run that pushed their lead back to nine before the half. Accordingly, Herro had to check back in to quell the run, matching Luka's 19-point half with 18 of his own. The Lakers would not slow down, though, and the Bucks went into the locker room down 50-61. Despite the hot-and-cold shooting, there was a lot to like from the first half, including the Bucks almost matching the Lakers' shot total (44 to 46) and matching the assist total with 14.

Both teams got off to a slow start in the third because of disruptive wing defence. The Bucks, however, were less effective at closing out on defensive possessions, which allowed the Lakers to get multiple shots per possession and turn the tide. Their lead grew to 17 by the 5:20 mark, and as Milwaukee announcer Marques Johnson alluded to, the Bucks were trying to hold on tight to a rope that kept gradually being pulled away. And yeah, that is what it felt like: Milwaukee didn't exactly give the game away, but they didn't help themselves either, with too many defensive rebounds slipping away. Other than Herro and Jaquez Jr., no other Bucks player reached double figures by the end of the third, and the Bucks were now well behind at 73-94.

Former Buck Sandro Mamukelashvili opened the fourth quarter with a driving layup to bring his point total to 23, proving to be a real difference-maker. Milwaukee just couldn't find its groove, shooting 2/11 through the first six minutes, with the deficit still hovering around 20. By then, the Bucks had scored just six second-chance points for the game (!) to the Lakers' 31, illustrating their lack of front-court presence. During garbage time, however, Milwaukee stitched together a 13-0 run, which at least showed some continued hustle from a young team, but it ultimately masked another blowout loss.

Nine: The number of first-quarter assists for the Bucks. For the rest of the game, the Bucks notched just 16.

The Bucks need a primary playmaker, and while the recent returns haven't been stellar, Milwaukee should consider starting Jakucionis to see if he can set the table and help others find their shots. There really isn't a single player who would not benefit from the Bucks having a primary playmaker; someone who can help control the tempo and distribute the ball. This year will be all about development, and the Bucks need to see if Jakucionis can fill a reliable true point guard role.

#2826. Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu emerges as potential host for 2027 Nations League final – report

Spain's bid to host the 2027 UEFA Nations League Final Four could give Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu a chance to host a major international event, with Valladolid's Jose Zorrilla Stadium also included in the proposed arrangement.

Spanish journalist Alfredo Martinez has reported through Defensa Central that UEFA is expected to favour the Spanish venues after considering other potential host countries, although it is crucial to note that the governing body has yet to announce its decision.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has formally submitted its hosting proposal, with Real Madrid and Real Valladolid involved in the preparations.

The timing is significant for the Bernabeu, as Real Madrid are increasingly positioning themselves as a venue for major international sporting events ahead of the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

RFEF president Rafael Louzan confirmed on September 27 that Spain had submitted its application to host the tournament's decisive stage.

Santiago Bernabeu could host the 2027 Nations League final. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

The proposed venues are the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid and Jose Zorrilla in Valladolid, with the Bernabeu expected to stage the final if Spain's bid succeeds.

Martinez explained the proposed arrangement: "The country has applied to host the tournament, and if the Spanish national team qualifies, they would normally be granted the opportunity.

"Furthermore, the other teams that could qualify have already hosted this phase in recent times: Italy, France, Portugal, and Germany. Therefore, Valladolid (Jose Zorrilla Stadium) and Madrid (Santiago Bernabeu Stadium) would be the venues for those matches."

Spain currently lead Nations League Group A3 with 12 points from four matches, having won all four of their opening fixtures.

They have already secured a place in the quarter-finals, but must still finish the group stage strongly to confirm their final position.

Real Madrid are also pushing to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Hosting the Final Four would give the national team an opportunity to compete for another international trophy after winning the World Cup earlier this year.

However, the hosting decision and Spain's eventual qualification for the final tournament remain separate matters.

For Real Madrid, the proposed Nations League hosting arrangement carries significance much beyond the competition itself.

This is because Spain is also campaigning to stage the 2030 FIFA World Cup final, and the Bernabeu is an obvious candidate given its capacity and international profile, although Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou is also in the running.

Indeed, hosting the Nations League final would not guarantee the Bernabeu the 2030 World Cup final, which remains a separate FIFA decision, although it is equally true that this competition could also strengthen the stadium's international credentials.

Someone's streak will come to an end Thursday night. Before the game tips off, here are a few things to know.

The Wolves have been without Anthony Edwards since he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery on October 29th. You might think that has slowed the Wolves down a bit, but in fact has not. Minnesota has won five of six without their franchise cornerstone, with four of the five wins being by double digits. Edwards averaged over 33 points per contest this season, and the Wolves have made up for it in a collective manner.

#2813. Mike Tomlin highlights 12 top coaching candidates for 2027 NFL offseason

The 2026 NFL season has reached its midpoint, and all 32 coaches who began the season in charge of their respective franchises remain in place.

As every NFL fan knows, that will not last long. Last season, 10 of the league's 32 teams made coaching changes. NFL owners are growing ever-impatient as they look to quickly build Super Bowl contenders, so leashes are shorter than ever for coaches.

That's why many will be on scorching hot seats during the second half of the season. And while none have been dismissed yet, a couple may fail to finish out the season, while numerous others will see their tenures end on "Black Monday," the day after the final game of the regular season.

But who will NFL owners and decision-makers be eyeing among the league's next crop of top coaching candidates? A few prominent retreads are on the market, along with the usual plethora of young, offensive-minded coaches.

Here's a look at the top coaching candidates to watch as the 2027 NFL coach hiring cycle draws ever nearer.
