#2726. Miami Heat Lock In 2028 All-Star Weekend Before Season Tip-Off

The NBA has already picked Miami to host the 2028 All-Star weekend, a league insider told The Associated Press on Monday. This decision comes before the current season has even reached its halfway point. A person with direct knowledge of the matter confirmed the selection several months ago.

Officials plan a formal announcement event on November 30 to reveal the site to the public. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver and Miami Heat chairman Micky Arison are expected to attend the ceremony. The logo for the event is already approved, and the bulk of the logistical planning is well underway.

It has been nearly 40 years since Miami last hosted the league's biggest midseason event. The city last played host in 1990, leaving a massive gap in its history. The delay happened because the All-Star weekend often clashed with a huge boat show in town. Organizers believed there simply was not enough hotel or event space to handle both big gatherings at once.

Tentative plans now call for some events to take place at the University of Miami's arena. Using multiple arenas for the weekend is a common practice across the league. The current All-Star weekend is scheduled to happen in Phoenix, but the focus has already shifted south.

The timing creates a unique story line if LeBron James plays in the 2027-28 season. James signed a two-year contract with the Philadelphia 76ers this past offseason. If he returns to the court in 2028, it would mark his 25th and likely final season.

That final season would mean his last All-Star weekend takes place in Miami. James spent four seasons with the Heat and won his first two championships there. He has a deep history with the city that goes beyond just playing on the court. The league knows this connection makes the location a perfect fit for a farewell tour.

The selection of Miami breaks a long drought for the franchise and the city. The 2028 weekend will be the first time the Heat host since the 1990 event. League officials say the biggest parts of the agreement are already in place. The announcement on November 30 will make the plans official for fans and players alike.

#2724. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2722. Opponent Breakdown: North Carolina Tar Heels Defense

Defense is Bill Belichick's forte, and the North Carolina Tar Heels are benefiting from his expertise this year. For the second straight year, Belichick has his defense ranked in the top 50 in yards per play. His group is being led by his son Brian after his son Steve left the team earlier this season. While the defense has taken a step back this year, they have played well enough to keep the Tar Heels in each game, and they've made big plays at big moments.

The most talented group on this team is the defensive line, with a couple of NFL prospects. Melkart Abou Jaoude is the returning ACC leader in sacks, while Jaylen Harvey has been a very good addition from Penn State with 21 pressures this season. The edges of this defense haven't put up crazy numbers from a havoc standpoint, but they will be key players for this defense if Louisville continues to attack the edges of the defense.

The interior of the line is where this defense is at its best. Xavier Lewis is one of the best defensive tackles in the country. He is in the top five in pressures, tackles for loss, and sacks among his position group. The 6-0/260 tackle is extremely undersized, but he is very quick, and he uses his quickness to beat blocks to get into the backfield. He will be a key player in this game and will likely cause some issues for Louisville's offensive line.

Isaiah Johnson and Leroy Jackson are the other top players on the interior of the defense. Jackson has 14 pressures on the season as the main backup for Lewis, but he and Johnson provide really good size on the inside as well. Johnson is big enough to demand a double team, which has been a factor in Lewis' big season. He has been able to get one-on-one matchups often, and that has not gone well for offensive linemen.

UNC's linebackers have benefited more than just about anyone from the strong play of the defensive line. Derek McDonald and Peyton Sheelmann are averaging 19 tackles a game between the two of them. Both players are ranked in the top 25 in tackles nationally, and they are constantly running free when you watch their games. Louisville has adapted their running game over the last few weeks, but they will likely have a hard time running the stretch zone runs that they really like. These two guys can run, and they will have a lot of space to get downhill to make tackles behind the line.

Jaiden Patterson leads a solid cornerback group that has played at an average level this season. UNC has given up a lot of yardage this season, but they are better when it comes to metrics like passer rating. The corners have had some issues against the top players they've seen this year. Umari Hatcher, Jordon Faison, Calvin Russell, and Bryant Wesco all stood out to me when I watched their games. Those receivers were able to get open and make big plays on the outside.

The biggest playmaker outside of the defensive linemen is Greg Smith at free safety. He leads the team with 3 interceptions this year, and he's at his best as a deep safety playing center field. Smith can also come down into the box in run support or cover if needed. He's having one of the best seasons in the ACC at safety. While this secondary isn't great, they do have a couple of players who can make a play on the ball, which is not something I would say about the last few opponents for the Cards.

#2721. District 3 football playoffs: Six Berks County teams fight to advance

Six Berks County football teams remain alive across four classifications. How many will stay in the hunt for a District 3 title?

With four teams earning first-week byes of the District 3 football playoffs, Exeter and Conrad Weiser got right into win-or-go-home territory, with both coming out victorious.

Both earned big wins and a boost of confidence, while the four other Berks teams enjoyed a much-needed week of rest after beginning their seasons in early August.

Now, heading into the second weekend of November, let's see who can keep the ball rolling and who will ultimately see their seasons come to an end.

Class 6A: No. 4 Wilson (8-2) vs No. 5 Harrisburg (9-2)

Out of all the Berks County teams that earned a bye, the Lancaster-Lebanon Section 1 champion Bulldogs may have needed it the most.

"Band aids and duct tape," Bulldogs coach Doug Dahms said, describing the team's situation as it deals with a boatload of injuries ahead of Friday's quarterfinal matchup.

There will be a lot of game-time decisions all around in West Lawn, which, at this point in the season, is something just about every team is dealing with in one way or another.

Among those dealing with injuries is Louisville commit Justice Hardy, who has appeared in just five games this season while battling a lingering shoulder injury since early September. He's another name who may or may not suit up Friday.

Hardy has just 231 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 38 carries out of the backfield.

Nonetheless, the Bulldogs are still loaded with talent, averaging 38 points per game while allowing just 12.

Senior Cole Peterson has thrown for 1,833 yards and 18 touchdowns, with his No. 1 target, James Madison commit Michael Glover, leading the team with 587 yards and six touchdowns.

Wilson is looking for its ninth district title after falling to Central York 42-7 in the semifinals last season.

The Cougars, loaded with talent on both sides of the ball, are coming off a 42-6 victory over William Penn in the first round. They're looking for their sixth consecutive Class 6A title.

The Cougars have been the Bulldogs' kryptonite in recent memory, with their championship streak beginning in 2021 when they beat Wilson 14-10, before defeating the Bulldogs again in 2024, 42-14.

The Cougars' defense has generated 21 takeaways, while the offense is led by quarterback Kayden Stephens, who has thrown for 1,557 yards and 18 touchdowns. They also have a weapon in the backfield in 6-foot, 1,000-yard rusher Princeton Dent.

The winner will play whoever comes out on top of No. 1 Central York against No. 9 Cumberland Valley.

Keys to victory: Play clean football. Limit penalties and turnovers. Wilson has committed 69 penalties for 666 yards (66.6 per game) and turned the ball over 18 times this season.

Class 5A: No. 1 Twin Valley (10-0) vs No. 9 Cocalico (7-4)

The Raiders have now completed back-to-back 10-0 regular seasons and will begin their postseason journey in search of another District 3 championship.

Last season, Twin Valley defeated Susquehanna Township 41-21 in Class 4A. Now, taking on a bigger beast in the 5A classification, will we see the same old Raiders?

Ranked fifth overall in 5A in the state according to Eric Epler of PennLive.com, Twin Valley will have a Week 10 rematch against Cocalico this week, the same team they defeated to secure the Section 3 title.

In that matchup, the Raiders won 28-9, with Maverik Foster rushing for 169 yards and three touchdowns.

Outgaining the Eagles 386-215, Cocalico's lone touchdown came in the third quarter on a 62-yard run by Jasiah Rios to make it a one-score game before a 14-point fourth quarter from the Raiders.

Twin Valley still has not allowed 100 total points this season, locking things down from the trenches to the second level, all the way back to the secondary.

What they've been able to accomplish is nothing short of impressive.

Offensively, Lucas Myers and Maverik Foster have combined for 1,723 yards and 29 touchdowns in 2026.

On the other side, the Eagles have four players, Rios, Rocco Rigney, James Anderson and Logan Horning, who have each rushed for over 600 yards and five touchdowns.

Cocalico will need exceptional performances from all of its playmakers if the Eagles want to get the job done this time around.

It's hard to beat a team twice in one season. Can the Raiders get it done and punch their ticket to the semifinals?

The winner will play whoever comes out on top of No. 4 Spring Grove and No. 5 Exeter, potentially setting up a rematch of the Raiders' Week 9 victory at Reiffton.

KEYS: Keep playing Twin Valley football. If it's not broken, don't fix it, and the Raiders are firing on all cylinders. Continue to pound the rock and put together another strong defensive performance.

Class 5A: No. 5 Exeter (9-2) vs No. 4 Spring Grove (8-2)

The Eagles have possibly hit their stride at the perfect time.

Following a tough 56-29 loss to Twin Valley in Week 9, Exeter has made their opponents pay since.

Winning the Lancaster-Lebanon League Section 2 title with a 23-13 victory over Conestoga Valley, the Eagles carried that momentum into a 40-19 win over Hershey in the first round at Reiffton.

Josh Jackson and Donovyn Alvarez have combined for 506 yards and seven touchdowns in those wins, running behind a strong upperclassmen-led offensive line.

The Eagles' defense has limited the big plays, even when facing backs with the talent to make them pay over the past two weeks. They've forced plenty of punts in the process, controlling the game on both sides of the ball.

Exeter is looking to make its fourth trip to the title game in 2026, having lost its last appearance to Bishop McDevitt in 2024, 48-14.

Up next is Spring Grove, a member of the South Central Atlantic Conference's Division 1. The Rockets are hot themselves, riding a five-game winning streak.

It'll be another matchup where both teams predominantly keep the ball on the ground.

Sophomores Brody Redding and Kade Gibbs have combined for 1,025 yards and 16 scores, while quarterback Davon Melbourne has added 724 yards and 10 touchdowns with his legs.

Melbourne has thrown for just 534 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions.

Defensively, senior Oliver Smith leads the team with 107 tackles.

The Rockets were knocked out of the playoffs by New Oxford, 31-26, in the quarterfinals last year.

KEYS: Control the time of possession and do not allow huge plays. Exeter started its last game with a nearly seven-minute drive. Sustaining those long possessions while limiting Spring Grove's ground game will be crucial.

Class 4A: No. 8 Conrad Weiser (7-4) vs No. 1 West York (10-0)

The Scouts are coming off a revenge game, earning a 20-6 win over ELCO in the first round after losing to the Raiders back in September.

Junior Kole Kupper returned to regular form with 139 yards and two touchdowns after being limited to just 68 yards in the first meeting. Kupper now has over 1,500 yards and 24 scores on the season.

The Scouts will need to bring their best in what will be their toughest test of 2026 as they travel to West York.

A member of the South Central Atlantic Conference's Division 2, the Bulldogs won the league title and are ranked No. 1 in the Class 4A state rankings according to Epler of PennLive.com.

West York has won three District 3 championships but was knocked out in the semifinals last season by Twin Valley, 45-14.

This year, averaging over 40 points per game while allowing fewer than 10 defensively, the Bulldogs are as well-rounded as it gets in high school football.

All-State quarterback Jensen Ferber is nearing the 2,000-yard mark, currently sitting at 1,937 yards and 22 touchdowns to just three interceptions.

Able to distribute the ball to a handful of different receivers, the Bulldogs have three players with more than five touchdowns.

The Scouts will have to get pressure on the pocket passer to have a chance in this one.

On the other side of the ball, the Bulldogs' junior defensive ends have wreaked havoc on opposing offenses.

Jamen Garnett and Logan Boyer each have 15 tackles for loss and have combined for 19, yes, 19 sacks.

Head coach Alan Moyer and the Scouts will have their hands full in all three phases of the game. They'll have to control the clock to keep Ferber off the field and wear down the junior edge rushers as much as possible.

The winner will play whoever comes out victorious between No. 4 Big Spring and No. 5 Lampeter-Strasburg.

KEYS: Control the clock and limit the Bulldogs' possessions. Getting Kole Kupper going will be the No. 1 priority if the Scouts want to pull off the upset.

Class 3A: No. 2 Schuylkill Valley (8-2) vs No. 3 Annville Cleona (7-3)

Two teams that have become very familiar with each other over the years will clash for the second time in three weeks.

And as stated before, it's not easy to beat a team twice in one season.

The Panthers will look to capitalize on that difficulty, as the Dutchmen dominated them in Week 10, earning a share of the Section 5 title in the process with a 56-21 win. Annville-Cleona outgained them 605-253.

Early on, the game was tied 14-14 in the second quarter. Then the slaughtering began.

Annville-Cleona's Yama Navarro, a 2,000-yard rusher, rushed for 411 yards and six touchdowns, leading a 42-0 run that busted the game wide open.

With another two weeks of preparation, head coach Bruce Harbach and his team will look to slow Navarro down by any means possible to have a chance at reaching the school's first-ever District 3 championship appearance.

Not only will the Panthers' defense need to step up in a major way, but senior quarterback Alex Aletras will need to put his best performance on display.

Aletras has thrown for 1,458 yards and 20 touchdowns to just two interceptions, while also leading the team in rushing with 623 yards and nine more scores.

The winner will play whoever comes out victorious between No. 1 Wyomissing and No. 4 Trinity in the Class 3A championship next week.

KEYS: Do not have a repeat of the Week 10 matchup. Slow down Yama Navarro by any means possible, and let Alex Aletras do what he does best: make plays.

Class 3A: No. 1 Wyomissing (7-2) vs No. 4 Trinity (6-4)

The Spartans will begin their postseason run in hopes of capturing their 13th District 3 title.

Back in Class 3A after two seasons in the 4A classification, Wyomissing had won five consecutive district titles before moving up.

In those two seasons, the Spartans fell in the championship to Lampeter-Strasburg, 30-27, in overtime, and lost 37-35 to Susquehanna Township in the semifinals on a last-second touchdown.

Now, after winning Section 4 two weeks ago, Wyomissing will take on last year's Lancaster-Lebanon postseason grim reaper: Trinity.

As the third seed, the Shamrocks defeated Schuylkill Valley, Annville-Cleona and then Berks Catholic to capture their second championship in four straight trips to the big game.

Another run-first team, Trinit, is led by 6-foot-3, 230-pound junior running back Brandon Harris. He has 1,276 yards, 18 touchdowns and seven 100-yard rushing games in 2026.

As for Wyomissing, ranked 10th in the state Class 3A rankings according to Epler of PennLive.com, fullback Ethan Nye has put together a string of strong performances out of the backfield.

The junior has scored nine of his 10 touchdowns in the final three weeks of the season, so look for head coach Bob Wolfrum to continue to ride Nye in the playoffs.

Senior Zander Westwood leads the team with 870 yards and will need a big performance as well if the Spartans want to advance this Saturday.

The Shamrocks average eight tackles for loss per game, which speaks to their ability to get after it in the trenches. The Spartans will have to stay on their assignments up front for all 48 minutes.

KEYS: Control the clock. It's what the Spartans do best.

Annville Cleona at Schuylkill Valley, 7 p.m.

#2720. Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup

Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers couldn't rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers.

They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4.

The Sixers' top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17).

The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley.

The Sixers' injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury.

With Friday's loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat.

The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland:

After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam.

The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers' Oct. 22 win over Cleveland, they were many levels below their best in the first quarter.

The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers' chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter.

Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid's larger problem was that he couldn't hit any sort of shot besides free throws.

He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds.

Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he's now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that's bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season.

Of course, it's notable that Embiid's been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We'll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out.

James didn't play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers.

As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc.

Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers' rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures.

With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland's lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass.

Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals.

Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers' comeback push.

The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk.

With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons, Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game.

Still, the Sixers' offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points.

Embiid didn't play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He's had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career, back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors.

Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they'd hit speed bumps throughout the year. They'll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

#2717. NFL midseason team grades include two A's and one F

The halfway point of the 2026 NFL regular season necessitates some midterm grades.

As the league enters the back half of the schedule, there's a clear sense of separation between the top contenders and the also-rans. Meanwhile, several teams have already sunk to the bottom, with seven organizations having two or fewer wins.

With nine weeks remaining, there's still a good deal of time for coaching staffs and players to reshape their fortunes. Still, the trends that emerged in the first two months of the season could be hard to shake.

Here are USA TODAY Sports' midseason grades for each team, with marks determined by how every franchise fared relative to the roster's capabilities and preseason expectations:

Kyle Shanahan's team remains the NFL's standard setter for efficiency and resilience. With injuries continuing to pile up in the receiving corps, San Francisco has still managed to get MVP-level play out of Brock Purdy while ranking first in EPA per play and second in points differential (+79). Health seems like the only thing that can truly trip the 49ers up late in the season, though a pass rush that hasn't registered a sack in the past two games will have to ramp up for Raheem Morris' unit to reach its full potential.

Amid what many saw as a potentially lost season, the Giants have found themselves. While some teams might have been sunk by losing their starting quarterback in Week 2, John Harbaugh's ingenuity paid off with the midseason acquisition and switch to J.J. McCarthy. The defense's cohesion despite the loss of Dexter Lawrence this offseason and Brian Burns to a torn anterior cruciate ligament should put coordinator Dennard Wilson on the short list for some head-coaching roles come January. Even if New York falls short of the NFC's contending class, Harbaugh has instituted some winning ways in a remarkably short window.

Under first-year coach Joe Brady, the Bills have tapped into a newfound sense of perseverance. The league's leading offense in yards per game (386.4) and scoring (32 points per game) has also set the bar for malleability, with Josh Allen able to transform the attack as needed to flatten opponents. Jim Leonhard's defense is still figuring things out on the fly, but the unit is coming up with enough game-flipping plays to sustain itself as it searches for a better sense of consistency.

After a trio of trade-deadline moves, there's no doubt that general manager James Gladstone and coach Liam Coen believe this team is a leading title contender. Should you? Maybe. At the very least, Jacksonville – which boasts the NFL's only triple-digit point differential (+108) – might be the league's most balanced team, ranking fifth offensively in EPA per play and second defensively. Trevor Lawrence looks fully in command of a system that allows him to wield any number of weapons on a given play, and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile's opportunistic group might lessen its reliance on splash plays after its midseason acquisitions. With a fairly forgiving schedule, however, it might not be clear until the playoffs whether Jacksonville truly can make a push for the organization's first Super Bowl appearance.

With Caleb Williams coming into his own, anything feels possible for Chicago. An already sky-high ceiling was pushed even higher with the trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who changes the entire complexion of the unit he just joined. Williams' four interceptions in an unnecessarily close call against the Buccaneers emphasized the volatility that might be in play for this team, but the Bears look capable of leaning on their defense in key stretches rather than relying on Ben Johnson's machine-like offense not to have its gears get jammed every once in a while.

Remember when people were trying to put Matt LaFleur on the hot seat? That dramatic September start now feels like a distant memory. The offensive equilibrium is difficult to trust, with Jordan Love having to generate explosive plays at the league's highest rate in order to compensate for a last-ranked rushing attack. But as LaFleur joked last week, "Well, you guys said you wanted to let him cook, so we're letting him cook." On the other side of the ball, Jonathan Gannon has done some of the best work of any coordinator this season, harnessing the aggressiveness of a unit that should step things up another notch once Micah Parsons returns.

For most teams, the 16 consecutive wins in one-score games would be a flashing sign for a forthcoming regression. At this point, though, it's difficult to write off Denver's late-game fortitude as a matter of mere luck. The Broncos' process, which has led to the team having the league's third-worst yardage differential, certainly looks to be lacking. But if Bo Nix and the rushing attack continue to make even incremental improvements, particularly on early downs, there might not be many tougher outs in the AFC.

A secondary prone to springing massive leaks still isn't fully in the clear. Despite being dealt a bad hand on the back end, however, Dan Campbell has managed to keep Detroit squarely in the NFC North hunt. The Lions will have to continue to be innovative defensively after largely standing pat at the trade deadline, though the offense also has to pick things up a bit after hitting a midseason lull.

Kenneth Walker III has certainly done his part in rejuvenating the run game and offense at large. There's a disturbing trend in play, however, with the explosive plays that fueled the 5-0 start eroding as of late. Kansas City might have to settle for its old ways with an aerial attack that operates primarily in the underneath area for yards-after-catch opportunities, but the offense still might have more flexibility than it did in previous years. The unpredictability of the pass rush and the kicking game loom as major points of concern.

Joe Burrow has pushed his way to the forefront of the NFL MVP conversation. Dexter Lawrence has turned the defensive line into a bunch of bullies at the line of scrimmage. What's not to like about Cincinnati's trajectory? The botched Arnold Ebiketie trade didn't reflect well on the organization's attention to detail, and the fallout could have a minor effect on the pass rush that's powering the defense. Overall, though, this feels like the Bengals team that everyone has been waiting to see after a three-year playoff drought.

This hasn't been the fully dominant title follow-up that some might have expected. Still, there's plenty of reason to believe another late-season surge could be in the cards. Sam Darnold's turnovers and injuries have compounded the problems of an offense that only looks right when it's feeding Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But with Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet both finally healthy, the ground game could be poised to take off. A defense that still smothers all of its opposition increases the margin for error and gives Seattle staying power down the stretch.

Mike McCarthy might not be producing much panache in Pittsburgh, but the Steelers are prevailing thanks to an efficient ground game and revitalized defense. In a conference where few teams seem truly reliable, this is at least a fairly trustworthy group. Though it seems inevitable that better competition will exploit the troubles Aaron Rodgers and the passing attack have in dealing with the blitz and trying to work deep downfield, the Steelers can count on clean play to keep them afloat in tight matchups.

Maybe this seems like a harsh mark for a group that was the NFL's last to suffer a loss and still is in the thick of the NFC North race at 6-2. But leadership continued to embrace this specific version of a build that necessitated a cheap solution at quarterback, and it whiffed there through the first half of the season. Waking from that delusion and grabbing Kirk Cousins at the eleventh hour was a necessary step to have any hope of salvaging the season, though the 38-year-old's presence only can do so much to assist a run game that's lagging behind where it should be.

Things have looked dire at times for the defending AFC champions, who have seen Drake Maye flounder in critical spots. New England has demonstrated it can escape those valleys, but this is still an outfit that's relegated itself to the fringe of the AFC playoff picture. Given the lack of help elsewhere in the receiving corps, the Patriots probably can't afford to have A.J. Brown be out of the lineup or a non-factor for much longer.

The bottom line of a 5-4 start sure looks good for a franchise that entered the year outwardly pushing scaled-back expectations after the Myles Garrett trade. Nevertheless, it's difficult to feel as though much of Cleveland's formula – which includes the 29th-ranked scoring attack and a -32 point differential – is sustainable. Deshaun Watson continues to weigh down an offense that can't overcome his limitations, which might be inhibiting the development of the young core. And Cleveland can't seem to shake its rampant mistakes, from penalties – no team has more than the Browns' 82 – to the missed tackles dogging a defense that struggles to stop the run.

Sean McVay said he's never faced a run of personnel hits in his 10 seasons as Rams coach like he has this season – and that was before Puka Nacua landed on injured reserve. That doesn't fully absolve the preseason Super Bowl favorites for how much of a letdown this campaign has been to date, though. Los Angeles is paying for a lack of receiver depth it was long warned about, and a team that's beat up on inferior foes looks ill-equipped to grapple with the likes of the 49ers and Seahawks down the stretch.

The Silver and Black's crash landing after a 3-0 start revealed a fundamental truth about the franchise: This roster is still a long way off from competing in the AFC West. Credit first-year coach Klint Kubiak with finding ways to try to mitigate the myriad shortcomings. But the midseason pivot to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza marked a fitting inflection point for a franchise that's now focused on reaping long-term rewards. The rookie quarterback, however, faces an inauspicious setup with a stalled-out run game and defense that has given up 30 or more points in five consecutive games.

This is going to be the grouping for the entirety of the NFC South, which seems stuck in football purgatory. Todd Bowles' defense, which now leads the NFL in EPA per play allowed, did a nice job righting the ship. But it remains to be seen whether offensive coordinator Zac Robinson can actually deploy Baker Mayfield as a value-added resource rather than something to be worked around, particularly after the quarterback's return from a dislocated right thumb. If anyone looks poised to take command of the league's most moribund division, however, it might be Tampa Bay.

Bryce Young finally brought out the explosive side of Carolina's offense. Then, everything else detonated for the Panthers, who are mired in a three-game skid. An iffy pass-protection setup has fully broken apart, with Young taking 14 sacks during the losing streak. The biggest disappointment, however, has been the unraveling of the defense. Perhaps the decimation of the injury-ravaged secondary was merely too much to overcome, but the decision to fire highly regarded coordinator Ejiro Evero on Oct. 30 demonstrated that the team clearly expected more out of this unit.

Atlanta briefly came back to life for what first seemed like an ill-fated three-week residency in prime time. But the Falcons have dropped four of their last five games, with a surprising takedown of the battered 49ers being the only outlier result during that stretch. It's fitting that a team led by Michael Penix Jr., the league's ultimate mystery-box quarterback, would prove so difficult to pin down. Trading away safety Jessie Bates III seems to indicate that general manager Ian Cunningham and president of football Matt Ryan believe the best iterations of this group are in the years to come.

A fairly uninspiring start to the season has served as a reminder that the worst-to-first projections were largely a reflection of the division rather than the Saints. Ultimately, Kellen Moore's crew doesn't have much to hang its hat on in Year 2 of the coach's tenure. Maybe the offense can reach a new level with running back Travis Etienne, who's played in just three games due to a hamstring injury, finally nearing a return.

In their surprising three wins to date, the Cardinals have proven themselves capable of punching above their weight class. That's an encouraging development in Mike LaFleur's first year, but there's still not enough of a clear core to have much confidence in what's been built to date. The final two months of the season might be a bit dodgier with Carson Beck taking over the offense, but at least a team with no clear path forward at quarterback will get a robust assessment of its third-round rookie.

What exactly can Dallas be confident about at midseason? It's certainly not the defense, which has made minor strides in recent weeks but still shows major vulnerabilities (including ranking last in third-down stop rate)? Meanwhile, the offense that was supposed to be the engine behind this group is stalling out with alarming frequency. Brian Schottenheimer's group has now authored two of the season's most embarrassing collapses and often shows a disregard for details. The Cowboys are somehow still a factor in the chase for the NFC East crown, but the wide-open nature of the division further underscores the missed opportunity here.

With a new regime driving home that wins and losses can't capture the progress of a teardown project, Miami makes for a difficult team to measure. At first glance, there aren't many areas that seem settled on a roster rife with holes. But first-year coach Jeff Hafley has clearly instituted a sense of determination in a group that, for all its deficiencies, hasn't lost by more than 10 points in a game since Week 3.

C.J. Stroud has slung Houston out of its early slump by propelling the team to wins in three of its last four games. Yet DeMeco Ryans' crew might still have too steep of a climb to re-enter the AFC playoff picture without some massive help. The dissolution of the back end of the defense is tough to swallow, while the offensive front's lack of push for a do-nothing ground game has left general manager Nick Caserio at a loss for answers. While surrendering the AFC South crown to Jacksonville last year felt like a possible one-season aberration, it now seems plain to see that Houston is no longer the class of the division.

More: Vikings' Kirk Cousins deal might doom NFC West: NFL trade deadline winners, losers

It's never a good sign when postgame news conferences become a matter of sussing out blame for late-game meltdowns. That's pretty much become the expectation for Washington, though. Dan Quinn and Co. have done little to wash away the foul taste of last season's disappointing follow-up to an NFC championship game run, leaving the distinct sense that this staff is on borrowed time, barring a sharp turnaround.

It's tempting to give Baltimore a pass on this season given how Lamar Jackson's injuries have derailed Jesse Minter's inaugural campaign. Yet the Ravens clearly were counting on a quick revival, and they've done little to support that cause. Minter hasn't brought the cohesiveness and cleanliness that were hallmarks of his Chargers defenses. In all, not nearly enough has changed in what was supposed to be a new era for the organization.

A calamitous run of injuries has unquestionably informed Philadelphia's ongoing seven-game losing streak. So, too, has the collapse of the infrastructure that once entrenched the Eagles as a lead NFC contender for the last half-decade. And personnel hits alone can't account for just how discouraging first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's system has been, with the run game never truly taking root. Good on Howie Roseman for seeing what's brewing and equipping himself with plenty of resources – 10 picks in the first two rounds over the next three years – for a reboot.

In hiring Robert Saleh and bringing on a horde of high-priced free agents, Tennessee seemed to be aiming for a rapid revival. Once that notion fizzled, the Titans seemed to embrace a longer timeline for establishing competitive relevance by trading away Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker. At least Cam Ward has finally exhibited some heartening progress, though the team can hardly feel settled about where things stand for the 2025 No. 1 pick.

At least they eventually concluded this season was a lost cause, even if that realization came about 10 months too late. Dropping general manager Chris Ballard and shedding several key contributors on expiring contracts were necessary measures for a rebooting team with limited draft capital. Keeping running back Jonathan Taylor, however, was an odd move for a franchise that no longer looks positioned to capitalize on his prime.

Sitting at 2-7, Aaron Glenn maintained this week that the Jets feel as though they're "right on the cusp of trying to break through." Some evidence of that supposed trajectory would be nice. Frustrations have led Garrett Wilson and Geno Smith to near their boiling points in recent weeks. Meanwhile, the defense Glenn intended to supercharge with his play-calling is on the brink of collapse after a disastrous October. Perhaps worst of all: Gang Green has an ugly track record of coming through when it counts, whether it's in the red zone or at the end of either half.

Did you ever imagine you might see Jim Harbaugh robbed of his joy when discussing football? That's the toll that the Chargers' 0-8 start has taken on their typically ebullient leader. It's still hard to square how a team that won 22 games in the first two years of Harbaugh's tenure has managed to bottom out so quickly, though offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme has been nothing short of a disaster for Justin Herbert and Co. Perhaps worst of all, however, is Los Angeles' aversion to pursuing any meaningful in-season change, from the refusal to enact a staff shake-up to the incomprehensible decision to hold firm at the trade deadline. With a clear deleterious effect in play, this season might not be able to be simply flushed by the organization once it's over.

#2716. Back in Philadelphia with Celtics, Paul George looks forward to ‘a regular game'

Back in Philadelphia with Celtics, Paul George looks forward to 'a regular game' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Paul George's presence back in town was one of the many swirling morning storylines at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

For good reason, former Celtics teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum will draw immense attention Tuesday night. After all, Brown has said there "might be a little lamb chops with some gravy" between the two, if not a full-blown beef.

But George's return to Philadelphia is more than a tiny subplot. Following two seasons in Philadelphia, he was the centerpiece of the Sixers' summer trade package to acquire Brown.

George told reporters before the Celtics' shootaround that it feels like "a regular game."

"Had I been here eight, nine, 10 years, different story," he said. "I was here two years. Obviously, we didn't have the best of luck or had a great, I think, partnership in terms of my ability to stay healthy and on the floor. So that kind of played into a lot of it.

"But obviously, it's a tremendous fan base, a great sports town to play in. So that was appreciated. There's no ill will for me. It'll be fun to just compete. And outside of that, it's a normal game."

The 36-year-old George indeed had trouble staying available for sustained stretches as a Sixer. He dealt with a variety of injuries and served a 25-game suspension last season for violating the NBA's anti-drug policy.

George did play well on both ends of the floor for much of the 2026 playoffs. He helped the Sixers come back to win a seven-game first-round series against the Celtics in historic fashion. The nine-time All-Star also brought a veteran steadiness to the Sixers' locker room and was glad to mentor younger players like VJ Edgecombe.

"Just his routine … even when he got hot, he didn't try to force it," Jabari Walker said Tuesday morning. "His game was smooth and I think that's how he is as a person, just not forcing anything and having a calm energy."

George has certainly enjoyed his early days as a Celtic.

Through nine games, he's averaged 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.3 steals while shooting 42.5 percent from three-point range. Boston will enter Tuesday night's matchup second in the Eastern Conference standings at 8-2, the Sixers first at 9-2.

"I've been kind of blown away," George said. "I think it exceeded my expectations since being in Boston. You never know how much culture is involved and how much culture changes your outlook on things and the effect it has mentally, physically, just being in an environment … and the culture that Boston presents.

"So I've been thrilled. I've been playing some of my best basketball of late, and just been enjoying grinding it out with these guys out here. It's a fun style of play and I can't talk (enough) about just the thrill, the happiness and the excitement and joy that it has brought being here."

He was asked what sort of reception he expects from Sixers fans.

"Not sure," George said. "In some ways, I helped land them a future piece for them. So with that, not sure how the reception would be."

#2715. Denny Hamlin Names 3 Races That Cost Him the 2026 Title, Blames Himself for 1

Denny Hamlin says three races cost him the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series title, and that one of the mistakes was his.

Hamlin looked back on the Chase on Actions Detrimental, his weekly racing podcast. He finished third in the final standings, 56 points behind champion Kyle Larson.

"We all know, right, that my Chase boiled down to two pivotal moments," Hamlin said. "Probably, I think in my mind, it was Las Vegas. Well, Darlington. Okay, okay, it's three. It's Darlington, it's Vegas, it's Phoenix, though."

"Those are the three tracks where we actually had winning speed. We were fast enough to win those, and those were where we got our worst results. And that is just a non-winning formula, right?" he said.

Darlington opened the Chase. A costly pit stop put Hamlin in traffic, and contact with Michael McDowell damaged his No. 11 Toyota. He finished 18th.

Hamlin does not think he caused that one. McDowell gave his side of the contact the following weekend, saying both drivers could have done better.

The October Chase race at Las Vegas was different. Hamlin said the team's pit call let Larson get back on the lead lap. Hamlin then spun while trying to regain ground.

"I didn't think I did anything wrong when I got hit by McDowell. I do think I did something wrong when I spun at Vegas," Hamlin said.

"But again, I was put in a tough spot, and then they were whipping the horse, saying, 'Go, go, go, get him.' And I'm like, 'All right, I'm gonna go.' And so, but that's still me," he said.

"They're not driving the car. I am," Hamlin said.

After Las Vegas, Hamlin defended his team over the pit call. Crew chief Chris Gayle explained the decision and took the blame for it.

At Phoenix, a tire failure ended a strong run. A pit-road speeding penalty also cost him a chance to get back on the lead lap, and he finished 28th. He still does not know what caused the tire to fail.

"And then the Phoenix tire, I mean, I don't know. Who knows? Is it us? Was it bad luck? I don't know," Hamlin said.

Hamlin entered the Chase as the top seed with a 25-point cushion after four regular-season wins for Joe Gibbs Racing. Under the new format, there were no elimination rounds, so every lost point carried forward.

He ran well in the finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway, winning Stage 2 and leading a race-high 87 laps. He finished sixth, while Larson clinched the title after Stage 1.

The 45-year-old has signaled that 2027 is likely his final full-time Cup season. He is still chasing his first Cup championship.

#2714. NHL Power Rankings: Flyers flounder to start new season as Rick Tocchet searches for answers

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Philadelphia opened the season with a 7-0 loss to the rival Pittsburgh Penguins, and coach Rick Tocchet described his team's play as "disturbing." There was only one way for the season to go after that, right? Wrong.

The Flyers are off to an 0-2-2 start, and the underlying numbers aren't pretty. Per Natural Stat Trick, they have a five-on-five expected goals share of 26.0%, which ranks last in the NHL. Their 4.57 xGA/60 also ranks last. Their 1.94 xGF/60? You guessed it. Last.

Tocchet's bunch entered the season with a lot of well-earned optimism. Even with subpar play from Matvei Michkov last season, the Flyers managed to reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2712. ‘Let's check the ball up': Jaylen Brown ready for first game against Celtics

'Let's check the ball up': Jaylen Brown ready for first game against Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jaylen Brown was asked Sunday whether he and Jayson Tatum had spoken since the former teammates addressed their relationship during the preseason.

Does he plan to approach Tatum before Tuesday night's game at Xfinity Mobile Arena?

"I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side," Brown said. "We're playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win. So it's nothing to talk about. Let's check the ball up."

After months of public comments, documentaries and questions about how their partnership ended, the basketball will finally take over.

Brown will face Boston for the first time since the Celtics traded him to Philadelphia for Paul George and four future draft assets in July. He spent his first 10 NBA seasons in Boston, played nine alongside Tatum and helped the Celtics win the 2024 championship, earning Finals MVP honors.

Tuesday's 8 p.m. game on NBC will also bring together the top two teams in the Eastern Conference. The Sixers are 9-2. Boston, riding a three-game winning streak, is 8-2 and sits a half-game behind Philadelphia.

"Another good opportunity for our team to be able to show what we're made of," Brown said. "I'm looking forward to it. Big-time matchup, two heavyweights in the East. Let's get it."

Brown has not hidden his appreciation for Boston, even as more has emerged about the deterioration of his relationship with Tatum and the organization.

"I love Boston," he said Sunday. "Boston's a great city. A lot of people I developed relationships with, you know what I mean? But I'm just focused on what's in front of me right now. And that's the most important thing."

He also acknowledged everything that accompanies an abrupt end to a decade with one organization.

"Decisions were made," Brown said. "It's life. It's business. Move on. It's OK. … It's emotions. You've got to pack up and move your stuff. Your family's got to pack up and move. But it's life. It's happened to numerous amounts of people, myself included.

"So I just look forward to being able to build with my team over here, trying to make the best of my situation."

Brown faced the Celtics during the preseason, but Tuesday will be the first meeting that counts. He said he did not know whether that would introduce emotions that were absent during the exhibition schedule.

"We'll see how I feel when we get out there," Brown said. "As of now, I've got no emotion toward nothing. So I'm just ready to go."

Tatum was similarly restrained after Boston's 117-97 victory over Milwaukee on Sunday.

"It's another game on the schedule," Tatum said. "It's the Celtics versus the Sixers. In the words of Brad Stevens, they all count as one."

Tatum called the Sixers "an incredible group" with a "great coaching staff," but declined to add to the discussion surrounding his relationship with Brown.

"Drama gets clicks and views," he said. "That's not my thing." CBS Sports reported Tatum's full comments Sunday night.

Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla was even more concise.

"It'll be fun," Mazzulla said. "It'll be a good atmosphere."

Brown is not the only centerpiece of the July deal who will face his former team.

George has settled quickly into Boston's lineup, averaging 20.4 points and supplying the high-volume outside shooting the Celtics have long prioritized. He scored 27 points and made five three-pointers Sunday as Boston beat Milwaukee for its third consecutive victory.

The Celtics have not needed George to duplicate everything Brown provided. He has fit alongside Tatum, Derrick White and Boston's returning core as another willing shooter and versatile defender.

Tatum is averaging 27.1 points, six rebounds and 7.8 assists. His playmaking has been especially important for a team that replaced Brown's downhill pressure with more shooting and ball movement.

Boston enters Tuesday ranked third in offensive rating and fourth in defensive rating. It is one of two NBA teams currently inside the top five on both ends of the floor.

The Celtics have also made 15.6 three-pointers per game, the second-highest average in the league. They set an NBA Cup record by hitting 24 against Charlotte on Friday, then made 18 more Sunday in Milwaukee.

That presents a clear challenge for a Sixers defense that has generally performed well but has occasionally surrendered clean perimeter looks after committing extra help toward the ball. Tatum, George, White, Payton Pritchard and Sam Hauser can all punish late rotations.

The Sixers have reached 9-2 without depending upon the same formula every night.

Tyrese Maxey leads them at 26.9 points per game. Brown is averaging 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds and four assists while shooting 47.7 percent from the field and 39.2 percent from three. Joel Embiid and LeBron James have supplied scoring, passing and defensive flexibility around them.

Brown has repeatedly described the team as unfinished despite its record.

"From our perspective, it's been some growing pains for sure, even though we've been able to win," he said. "The result, we're not so much fixated on the result. It's more so about the process, and we've got to improve our process and our mentality to creating a winning environment."

Boston should provide the clearest early measure of that process.

The Celtics play considerably slower than the Sixers, but their half-court execution has been more efficient. Philadelphia will want to create turnovers and run before Boston can set its defense. The Celtics will attempt to control the pace, generate three-pointers and make the Sixers execute against a defense that has yet to allow an opposing player to score 30 points this season.

There is also the unavoidable Brown matchup. Boston could use Tatum, George and White against him at different points, giving the Celtics several defenders capable of absorbing his drives without immediately sending help.

Nick Nurse expects Brown to bring something extra, even if Brown has publicly downplayed the emotional component.

"It's going to be very different for him," Nurse said. "I think probably a little bit of emotion in there, too, but also I think he's going to be very motivated to play."

Boston's rotation is healthy entering the matchup. Two-way guard Devin Carter is out because of an illness.

Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti remain out for the Sixers. Adem Bona could return after missing Sunday's contest.

The betting market views the matchup as essentially a toss-up. Monday afternoon listings had the spread moving between Boston minus-1.5 and Philadelphia minus-1.5, depending on the sportsbook, with the total at 215.5.

That fits the larger picture. Philadelphia owns the East's best record. Boston has the conference's strongest point differential and has outscored opponents by 10.7 points per game.

The surrounding conversation will center on Brown and Tatum until the opening tip. Brown does not intend to contribute any ceremonial small talk.

"He's on his side," Brown said. "I'm on my side."

#2708. Bilal Hasan says only human nature to get on his hype train at UFC 334

NEW YORK – In some respects, even Bilal Hasan might cop to being tossed into hypebeast mode.

Hasan, an unbeaten flyweight, has risen quickly thanks to a highlight-reel win on DWCS, and a turnaround less than three weeks later for a UFC debut that left him with an extra $100,000 in his pocket.

Throw in the 25-year-old Hawaiian's love of the legendary "King of Pop," Michael Jackson, and the likelihood he'll add a moonwalk to a post-fight celebration, and he's just off the wall enough to be overhyped in the wrong hands. Saturday, he'll have his most high-profile shot yet at becoming the next thriller at 125 pounds.

Hasan (10-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC) takes on Luis Gurule (11-4 MMA, 1-4 UFC) to open up the main card at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. That card placement at MSG, on a card with two title fights, is something Hasan thought would happen – but down the road.

"This is exactly what I expected, just not at this rate," Hasan told MMA Junkie and other reporters at Wednesday's UFC 334 media day. "The UFC put me on a rocket ship, and I'm here enjoying every moment. I just truly believe that this is such a great position to be in, and it's very unique. This is a true privilege for me to be here.

"At first, I wanted a slow buildup, but the UFC sees potential in me. I've believed in myself since Day One, so I'm just going to ride this rocket ship."

Against Gurule, he'll be up against his most accomplished opponent yet. Hasan beat Nilson Rojas in his UFC debut in August, and though Rojas was unbeaten, he was making his UFC debut. Gurule, Hasan admits, isn't going to set the neon ablaze with his 1-4 record in the promotion, either.

And that, he knows, puts him in position to be upset. He's as much as a 12-1 betting favorite, by far the biggest on the card.

"I've seen him fight before. He's a veteran in the UFC – not the best record, but he's fought very tough prospects in this division," Hasan said. "I don't really see anything special. I think he knows what he needs to do to try to get the victory, but it's the perfect stylistic matchup for me to go out there and put on another highlight performance and get another performance bonus."

Hasan said Gurule's mentality – that he's out to send his opponent's proverbial trolley of hype barreling off the tracks – seems like a natural reaction.

"If I was in his position, I'd probably say the same thing," Hasan said. "But I also know if I was in his position and seeing not only the highlights that I put on, but how much the UFC backs me – it's a lot. I can't imagine the pressure on his shoulders.

"But I think this is just going to be a theme in my career. I truly believe people's eyes are all on me and they're going to try to derail this hype train, and I'm going to go in there and enjoy the moment. I feel like I'm the best when I'm present and truly enjoying myself, so that's what I'm planning to do Saturday night."

#2707. Must Cs: Celtics complete 7-point possession during 16-0 run in Toronto

On the second night of a back-to-back and without Paul George (illness), the Celtics fell into a trap game with home just a puddle jump away after a four-game road trip. After the high of Tuesday night's blowout of the 76ers and arriving in Toronto at 4 am, Boston found themselves behind the 8-ball early in the game facing a 22-point deficit midway through the second quarter.

A 7-0 Jayson Tatum run with a pull-up three, two free throws, and a thunderous dunk led to a Toronto timeout and then the unthinkable happened.

Tatum struck again with a killer triple with Collin Murray-Boyles slipping under JT's feet for a flagrant foul. After hitting the free throw, Baylor Scheierman hit another catch-and-shoot 3 to complete the rare SEVEN-POINT possession.

For what it's worth, the only other seven-point possession I can remember was in the 2022 NBA Finals when Al Horford fouled Steph Curry on a 3 and then Otto Porter hit another after Curry went to the free throw line.

This slick fastbreak capped off the 16-0 run in two and a half minutes.

In the end, the Celtics completed their second largest comeback in Joe Mazzulla's tenure as head coach. Down six with five minutes to go, Boston closed with a 13-4 run with some lockdown defense, gritty play on both sides of the ball from Neemias Queta, and Tatum getting to the line. However, it was that first half stretch that really made the difference in sweeping their road trip.

"His energy just lifted everybody," Mazzulla said of Tatum's presence during that crucial run. "It's the same thing when you lose close games. We didn't win the game in the fourth quarter. We won the game in the middle of the second quarter when we cut it to seven again."

#2706. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2705. Broncos, Giants, Browns among teams proving that winning ugly might be good enough this season

Everyone wants to be the mid-1980s 49ers or 1999 Rams, blowing teams out and making their seasons into beautiful highlight reels.

In the NFL in 2026, that might not be possible. Just grinding out wins is good enough.

There are four teams this season who have a winning record despite a point differential of +12 or worse: Broncos, Giants, Patriots, Browns. The Browns are 5-4 despite a point differential of -35. The Broncos have won seven games and six of them came by one score. They barely beat the 0-7 Chargers in Week 5 after trailing with less than 10 minutes remaining.

But they're winning. All of those teams would be in the playoffs if they started today other than the Browns, who are one spot out of an AFC wild-card spot. Other teams like the Steelers and Packers haven't been impressive from Week 1 on, but they're in the playoff field too.

"We found a way to win," has been uttered more than a few times by head coaches of winning teams this season. Winning ugly might end up being the theme of this season.

Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants and Tyrone Tracy Jr. embrace after an overtime win over the Texans in Week 5.

The Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 sums up how a handful of teams are succeeding this season. The Giants got four field goals and their only touchdown came when Jameis Winston came in off the bench for a drive. From an outside perspective, it was an unwatchable game. But it was pretty good for the Giants.

"We did play winning football, not perfect football, but winning football and found a way to win the game in all three phases, especially starting with the defense," Giants coach John Harbaugh said, via Athlon Sports.

The Giants beat the Titans, who are 1-7, when they intercepted a pass in their own end zone in the final seconds. They beat the Cardinals, who are 3-6, when they intercepted a pass backed up in their own end zone on the final play. The Giants rank 24th in DVOA but are currently the No. 3 seed in the NFC with a 5-2-1 record. For old-school football fans who abhor analytics and care only about a team's record, there's satisfaction in teams winning in intangible ways.

"They have it. They have what it takes," Harbaugh said of his team. "I don't know how to describe it other than that. I think they've had it all along and they found it in these games. Sometimes it's one thing to have it and another thing to find it, and they've been able to find it in the way they play."

The Browns are one spot below the Giants in DVOA, ranking 25th. But they've won more than they've lost. In multiple games this season they've discovered the right answer to the test in the final minutes. In four of five wins they've trailed or been tied in the final two minutes, and in the other win they trailed with four minutes remaining. They're 3-2 in games in which they gain 272 yards or less.

"We don't do anything, and then all of a sudden we get stops," Monken said after a 13-10 win over Baltimore, via the Ravens' site. "All of a sudden we figure it out."

These teams are chasing playoff berths, not trying to hear arguments about regression.

Since the start of the 2025 season, the Broncos are on one of the strangest runs in recent NFL history.

The Broncos are 22-6, counting postseason, and 18 of the wins have come by one score. For those who understand probability, and one-score games in the NFL being practically a coin flip, that record makes no sense.

The Broncos are 7-2 with a point differential of +12. That might be unsustainable, but they did it last season, too. The Broncos have won 16 one-score games in a row, setting an NFL record. That can't continue, but the Broncos truly believe it can.

"Well, when it keeps happening, I think our league is what it is," Broncos coach Sean Payton said after a 26-21 win over the Panthers. "When those things keep falling your way, that's not by accident."

Other teams looked terrible in September and have emerged as contenders for division titles. Packers fans had Matt LaFleur on the hot seat after a bad Thursday night loss to the Falcons dropped them to 1-2. The Steelers were 2-2 after four games and didn't look anything like a playoff contender, but haven't lost since. The Patriots were in trouble at 1-2 and while a blowout loss to the Packers last week was a setback, they're above .500 despite a win differential of just +4.

There might not be a more oft-used quote in the NFL than Bill Parcells' famous line, "You are what your record says you are." And, in truth, the win-loss record is all NFL coaches and players are judged upon. So nobody with a winning record now is making apologies, even if all those victories haven't been pretty.
